R2 RETROFIT — decoder model header in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5 (branch claude/h100-audit-maximal, H100 sm_90a). Mission: convert the decoder cell's per-sample scalar GEMMs to batch-tiled bf16 wgmma using the COMMITTED substrate, as a TUNED VARIANT alongside the scalar path. The decoder cell is silicon-validated (grok 3/3, parity green) — your work must keep that true.

READ FIRST: DESIGN-TC-PIPELINE.md (the implementation contract: Fork B dW-output-stationary, smem budgets, barrier counts); csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/wgmma.cuh + tile_pipeline.cuh — the validated API; HEADLINE TRAP documented in wgmma.cuh: operands MUST be staged canonical Major-K core-matrix idx(mn,k)=(k/8)*(MN*8)+mn*8+(k%8); N<=128 per call (tile loop for wider), TILE_M stacks m64 atoms (unexercised — you exercise it first). Reference structure: csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stages_decoder.cuh (the scalar fwd/bwd, oracle-validated; ld* stride contracts) + fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh (P0..P3 driver) + decoder_layout.cuh.

DESIGN (per design doc — its decisions are the contract):
- New header csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh: batch-tiled bf16 wgmma fwd+bwd: activations [T=B*4 tokens x 128] bf16 in HBM (fp32 master weights converted once per step into bf16 smem tiles); layer-by-layer GEMMs with grid barriers between (no CUDA graphs); attention scores per-sample remain scalar fp32 (seq=4 tiny — design doc's call); softmax/LN/CE fp32 per autocast policy; Fork B dW-output-stationary (CTAs own dW tiles, contract full T) eliminating the per-CTA partial workspace; deterministic fixed k-order; embedding scatters stay owner-deterministic.
- Driver/cell: SG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL selects scalar|wgmma path (BOTH compiled; tuner picks per cell — owner directive). Tile shapes/pipeline depth via the substrate's SG_TUNED_* macros. New cell TU mega_decoder_real_adamw uses the dim — keep the dispatch.cpp signature identical (no bindings.cpp).
- VALIDATION (NON-NEGOTIABLE, each gate): wgmma path vs eager-bf16 — bf16 tolerances (~2e-3 class, derive from accumulation; the fp32 path's gates stay UNCHANGED + green); 30/30 grads vs fp64 oracle bf16-rounded; trajectory chaos-calibrated; determinism bit-exact; refuse-not-hang; SASS HGMMA present. Run tests with CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent (standing rule).
EDIT SCOPE: new files (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh, test_decoder_tc.py) + minimal SG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL ifdefs in fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh + mega_decoder_real_adamw.cu. Do NOT touch compile.py (sibling writing), dispatch.py/cpp, bindings.cpp, model_stages_decoder.cuh math, optimizer headers. No suppression; full rebuilds OK (~10 min). Don't commit.
REPORT: per-gate numbers, achieved step-time vs scalar (rough, contended ok), smem/regs, deviations, the contract vit/mamba TC ports copy.

1	# DESIGN-TC-PIPELINE.md — Tensor-core batch-tiled megakernel (R2) implementation contract
2	
3	**Scope.** Branch `claude/h100-audit-maximal`, H100 sm_90, CUDA 12.4. Performance
4	architecture for the persistent-megakernel race cells (3 models × 11 optimizers =
5	33 L3 cells). Target: **maximize roofline fraction per cell** under the owner's
6	constraints (bf16 race precision with fp32 accum; no CUDA graphs — one persistent
7	kernel + in-kernel grid barriers; deterministic — no float atomics, fixed
8	reduction order; hang-free — occupancy ≥ 1 or refuse; maximal verified PTX).
9	
10	**This is an implementation contract for a build agent.** Every optimization lands
11	inside a component layer (substrate / model-stage header / optimizer header /
12	`opt_components.cuh`) so all 33 cells inherit it through recomposition by
13	`megakernel_codegen.py`. No cell-specific hacks. The architecture in
14	`csrc/fused/COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md` is inviolate.
15	
16	**Honesty rails.** Where my context notes contradict the code, the **code wins**
17	and is cited `file:line`. Every number is sourced or computed (arithmetic shown).
18	Achievable roofs are shape-honest — no "wgmma → peak" claims. Uncertainties are
19	flagged 🟡.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 0. Corrections to the briefing (code wins)
24	
25	| Briefing claim | Code reality | Source |
26	|---|---|---|
27	| decoder full-batch "~4.7k samples ≈ 4191" | **B = int(97²·0.5) = 4704** samples; the `4191` in code comments is a stale val-split number, not the train batch | `grokking_race_v2.py:238` (`frac_train 0.5`, `p 97`); verified `int(97*97*0.5)=4704` |
28	| decoder "vocab 97/99" | tok-embedding rows **99**; CE over **99** logits | `decoder_layout.cuh:23` `SG_DEC_VOCAB=99` |
29	| decoder megakernel "3 phases / 2 barriers" | current decoder cell is **4 phases / 3 grid barriers**: P0 zero → **B0** (`:124`) → P1 fwd+bwd → **B1** (`:148`) → P2 reduce → **B2** (`:178`) → P3 opt. (The file's own docstring at `:18` says "5 phases / 4 barriers" but enumerates only P0–P3 and B0–B2 — the docstring is stale; the **call sites** are the ground truth.) | `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:124,148,178` |
30	| mamba "d_inner 256, 259,425 params" | confirmed: **28 tensors, 259,425 elems**; smem **145,124 B** dynamic | `mamba3_layout.cuh:40-41,116` |
31	| vit "418,017 params, 17 pos" | confirmed: **32 tensors, 418,017 elems**; smem **188,080 B** dynamic | `vit_layout.cuh:46-47,137` |
32	| "wgmma machinery exists / warpgroup utils" | **No in-kernel wgmma anywhere.** Every model-stage GEMM is a **scalar fp32 owner-computes triple loop** (`dec_linear`, `vit_linear`, `mb_linear`). The only WGMMA path is **host-launched CUTLASS** in `mma.cuh` (not device-callable). `wgs::` has mbarrier / setmaxnreg / elect only — no MMA. cp.async + DSMEM-reduce + L2-persist exist in `primitives.cuh`; **TMA tensor-map / `cp.async.bulk.tensor` do NOT exist** | grep: only hit for `wgmma` outside `mma.cuh` is `compile.py` (a feature-detect string); `model_stage_*` scalar loops at `dec_linear` `model_stages_decoder.cuh:289`, `vit_linear:299`, `mb_linear:307` |
33	
34	**Consequence of the last row** — this is the design's pivot and is developed in §1.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 1. The regime, and the two architectural forks (read this first)
39	
40	### 1.1 The regime split: current = memory-bound; post-R2 decoder/vit = compute-bound; mamba = memory-bound. Verified.
41	
42	The current scalar cells are memory-bound (on the 223 MB partial workspace, §1.2).
43	After Fork B removes the partials (§3), the **decoder and vit move COMPUTE-bound**
44	(decoder AI ≈ 900 FLOP/B ≫ the 295 FLOP/B bf16 ridge — §10.4), so their roof is
45	GEMM-limited and the §3 short-K/occupancy=1 achievable-roof honesty is what governs.
46	**Mamba stays memory-bound** intrinsically (the selective scan, AI ≈ 0.86 FLOP/B —
47	§8). The compute floors below set the prize; the per-GEMM roofs (§3) set what is
48	actually reachable.
49	
50	Decoder fwd+bwd FLOPs/step (computed — `python3`, shown):
51	- per-layer MACs = in_proj(S·3d·d) + scores(H·S·S·dh) + ctx(H·S·dh·S) + out_proj(S·d·d) + ff0(S·dff·d) + ff2(S·d·dff); head(1·V·d).
52	- fwd = L·per_layer + head = **1,593,728 MAC/sample**; bwd ≈ 2× fwd (dX + dW) ⇒ fwd+bwd = 3× fwd = **9,562,368 FLOP/sample** (MAC=2 FLOP).
53	- × B=4704 ⇒ **44.98 GFLOP/step** (matches the briefing "tens of GFLOP").
54	
55	| precision | peak (TF/s) | decoder compute floor / step |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| bf16 TC | 989.4 | **45.5 µs** |
58	| tf32 TC | 494.7 | 90.9 µs |
59	| fp32 CUDA | 66.9 | **672 µs** |
60	
61	Source peaks: `tuning/roofline.py:44-54`.
62	
63	**The current scalar fp32 design is pinned near the 672 µs CUDA-core floor and in
64	practice far below it** (one sample per CTA, no ILP, no vectorization, no TC).
65	The bf16-TC floor is **14.8× below** the fp32-CUDA floor — that gap is the prize.
66	
67	### 1.2 But the dW partial workspace already costs 3× the bf16 floor
68	
69	The current cells use a `[nCTA × total]` per-CTA grad-partial buffer
70	(`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:112` `tok.workspace + cta*total`), reduced in P2:
71	- nCTA=132 (H100 SMs), total=422,755, fp32 ⇒ **223 MB**.
72	- P1 writes it, P2 reads it ⇒ **446 MB / step → 133 µs** at HBM3 3.35 TB/s.
73	
74	**133 µs is ~3× the 45 µs bf16 compute floor.** So even a perfect TC GEMM leaves
75	the decoder cell memory-bound on the partials alone. **Q2 (eliminate the partials)
76	is co-primary with Q1 (the TC restructure), not a follow-up.** The same holds for
77	vit (132×418,017×4 = 221 MB) and is the dominant cost for mamba (132×259,425×4 =
78	137 MB; mamba's GEMMs are already memory-bound — §8).
79	
80	### 1.3 The Q1/Q2 duality — you cannot eliminate both global acts AND partials
81	
82	This is the load-bearing constraint the whole doc is organized around.
83	
84	- The full token tensor does **not** fit smem: T·d·2B = 18,816·128·2 = **4.8 MB ≫
85	  227 KB**. So "activations smem-resident" is only ever achievable **per-CTA on a
86	  token-tile**, never globally.
87	- The weight-grad contraction dW = Xᵀ@dY sums over the **token dimension T**,
88	  which is **spread across CTAs** (each CTA owns a token slice). Therefore:
89	  - **Either** acts stay CTA-local in smem (a token-tile) **and** dW needs a
90	    **cross-CTA reduction** (→ the partials, 223 MB),
91	  - **or** dW is **output-stationary** — each CTA owns dW tiles and contracts the
92	    **full T itself** (Q2, no partials) — **but then acts must live in HBM** so the
93	    dW-owning CTA can read every token's activation.
94	
95	You get one or the other per GEMM, chosen by traffic. Naming this duality is the
96	honest answer to Q1+Q2; "both at once" is impossible.
97	
98	**Fork A — CTA-local token-tile (M_tile≈128), wgmma on the local tile, keep the
99	current recompute-in-bwd discipline.** No global acts; no new inter-layer grid
100	barriers (a CTA stays local through all layers, exactly as today). **But dW still
101	needs the cross-CTA reduction → keeps the 223 MB partials (133 µs).**
102	
103	**Fork B — dW-output-stationary (Q2).** Eliminates the 223 MB partials. fwd writes
104	acts to HBM; bwd dW-tile CTAs stream the full T. Acts traffic (decoder, bf16,
105	rough): ~2 `[T,d]` tensors/layer × L = 9.6M elems × 2B × (write+read) = **39 MB →
106	11.5 µs** (computed). vit/mamba scale with d_inner but stay tens of MB in bf16.
107	
108	**Recommendation: Fork B for all three models.** 39 MB (11.5 µs) of acts traffic
109	replaces 446 MB (133 µs) of partials traffic — an **11× traffic reduction on the
110	dominant term**, and it deletes one whole grid-barrier phase (P2 reduce, B1). The
111	acts round-trip is the documented cost; it is an order of magnitude smaller than
112	the partials it replaces. Fork A is retained only as the fallback for any GEMM
113	whose dW output tile is so small that output-stationary under-occupies (none in the
114	race — see §3).
115	
116	> **Note on the briefing's Q1 phrasing.** The briefing's "layer-by-layer batched
117	> GEMMs across T with a grid barrier between each layer GEMM, acts in HBM" is one
118	> realization of Fork B, but **a global per-layer barrier is NOT mandatory** and is
119	> rejected: it would serialize the grid L×(#GEMMs) times per step. The chosen
120	> structure (§2) keeps each CTA's fwd→bwd **local and barrier-free within the
121	> token-tile**, with grid barriers only at the genuine cross-CTA couplings
122	> (embedding scatter, optimizer). Code/analysis wins over the context note.
123	
124	---
125	
126	## 2. The persistent-kernel phase structure (Fork B), per step
127	
128	One launch, gridDim = #SMs, 256 threads/CTA (two Hopper warpgroups). Barriers are
129	the existing `GridBarrier::sync` / `sync_reset` (`megakernel_common.cuh:144,209`).
130	
131	```
132	P0  zero embedding-grad accumulators (tok/pos only — the ONLY tensors needing a
133	    cross-CTA scatter; all weight dW are output-stationary so need no pre-zero).
134	--- B0 (sync_reset) ---
135	P1  FWD+BWD, token-tile-parallel. Each CTA owns a contiguous token-tile of M_tile
136	    rows (M_tile=SG_TUNED_TILE_M, default 128). For its tile it runs the full
137	    fwd then bwd through all layers, wgmma on bf16 smem tiles, fp32 accumulators.
138	      - forward activations needed by bwd are written to HBM acts[T, ...] (bf16)
139	        OR recomputed (the current recompute discipline still applies per tile).
140	      - dW: each CTA accumulates its tile's contribution into its OWNED dW output
141	        tiles by contracting its M_tile rows; see §3 for the split-K ownership that
142	        makes this a full-T contraction without partials.
143	      - embedding grads (tok/pos): index-scatter into the P0 accumulators by the
144	        deterministic owner map of §3.4.
145	      - loss: per-CTA fp32 NLL slot (kept — `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:147`).
146	--- B1 (sync_reset) ---
147	P2  OPTIMIZER tail. apply_optimizer<Opt> over the (now-complete, in-place) grad.
148	    For epilogue-fusable optimizers (§4) this phase is FUSED INTO P1's dW epilogue
149	    and B1+P2 collapse — 3 phases / 2 barriers for adamw/lion/grokfast/grokadamw/
150	    neuralgrok. Non-fusable optimizers keep P2 (and their own precompute phases).
151	```
152	
153	**Barrier count per step, decoder, before vs after:**
154	
155	| design | phases | grid barriers |
156	|---|---|---|
157	| current (scalar, partials) | 4 (P0,P1,P2-reduce,P3-opt) | **3** (B0,B1,B2; the fwd→bwd sync inside P1 is `__syncthreads`, not a grid barrier) |
158	| Fork B, non-fusable opt | 3 | **2** |
159	| Fork B, **epilogue-fused opt** (5 of 11) | 2 | **1 or 2** (see caveat) |
160	
161	The dW-reduce phase (P2) + its barrier (B2) are **deleted** (no partials → nothing
162	to reduce): the baseline **3 → 2** barriers, a net saving of **one** grid barrier.
163	This is the second win of Fork B beyond traffic.
164	
165	> **Embedding caveat on the "1 barrier" fused case.** Weight dW fuses to its
166	> optimizer in the P1 epilogue (0 extra barriers). But the **tok/pos** grads are a
167	> cross-CTA scatter (§3.4) that every CTA contributes to — their optimizer apply
168	> must wait for **all** CTAs to finish scattering, which needs **B1 before the
169	> tok/pos apply**. So a fully-epilogue-fused cell is **2 phases / 1 barrier for the
170	> ~28 weight tensors, but the 2 embedding tensors still require that one barrier** —
171	> i.e. the realistic fused floor is **1 barrier (B0 for the embedding-accumulator
172	> zero + the post-scatter rendezvous folded into it)**, not zero. The 5-fusable
173	> cells land at **1 barrier**; do not claim 0. 🟡
174	
175	> 🟡 **Recompute vs acts-in-HBM is itself a per-model choice.** Decoder's bwd
176	> currently recomputes each layer from `layer_in` (`model_stages_decoder.cuh:498`
177	> `dec_recompute_layer`) to stay under 48 KB static smem. Under Fork B the dW CTA
178	> needs *other* CTAs' tile activations, so the cross-tile activations MUST be in
179	> HBM regardless; the within-tile recompute can stay. The build agent picks
180	> recompute-vs-store per GEMM by the smem budget table (§6/§9); both are
181	> bit-identical in the produced grad (same expression, different storage class).
182	
183	---
184	
185	## 3. Per-GEMM TC plan (M/N/K, wgmma tiling, ownership, achievable roof)
186	
187	Conventions: wgmma atom `m64nNk16` for bf16 (Hopper ss-wgmma; N ∈ {8..256}). A
188	"CTA tile" is the M×N output block one CTA owns; the K loop iterates k-steps of 16.
189	Activations are bf16 in smem staged from HBM via cp.async (TMA in phase-2, §4).
190	**Achievable roof per GEMM is bounded by the mainloop k-step count** (short-K = few
191	MMA issues to amortize prologue/epilogue + occupancy=1 has no inter-CTA latency
192	hiding — the in-CTA producer/consumer pipeline must hide it). I give the roof class
193	honestly; I do **not** claim peak.
194	
195	### 3.1 Decoder (d=128, dff=512, S=4, V=99, H=4, dh=32; B=4704, T=18,816)
196	
197	The forward GEMMs are tall-skinny in T: **M = number of (sample×position) rows the
198	GEMM touches.** in_proj/out_proj/ff act on all S positions ⇒ M-rows = T = 18,816.
199	The head acts on the last position only ⇒ M-rows = B = 4704.
200	
201	| GEMM | M (rows) | N | K | wgmma tiling | CTA tile (M×N) | acts location | roof class |
202	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
203	| **in_proj** (fwd) qkv = X·Wᵀ | 18,816 | 3d=384 | d=128 | m64n128k16, 3 N-tiles, **8 k-steps** | 128×128, ~147 M-tiles over 132 SMs | X in smem tile (bf16) | K=128 → mid. M huge → TC-saturated on issue; **~55–70%** 🟡 |
204	| **scores** q·kᵀ (per head) | S=4 | S=4 | dh=32 | **too small for wgmma** — 4×4×32. Keep **scalar fp32** per (head,qrow) exactly as now (`model_stages_decoder.cuh:364`) | — | smem | N/A (special-cased; <0.1% of FLOPs) |
205	| **ctx** attn·v (per head) | S=4 | dh=32 | S=4 | too small — scalar fp32, kept | — | smem | N/A |
206	| **out_proj** a = ctx·Wᵀ | 18,816 | d=128 | d=128 | m64n128k16, **8 k-steps** | 128×128 | smem tile | as in_proj, **~55–70%** 🟡 |
207	| **ff0** g = x1·Wᵀ | 18,816 | dff=512 | d=128 | m64n128k16, 4 N-tiles, **8 k-steps** | 128×128 | smem tile | M·N large; **~60–72%** 🟡 |
208	| **ff2** ff = g·Wᵀ | 18,816 | d=128 | dff=512 | m64n128k16, **32 k-steps** | 128×128 | smem tile | **best — K=512 amortizes prologue; ~72–82%** 🟡 |
209	| **head** logits = hn·Wᵀ | 4704 | V=99 | d=128 | m64n96k16 (pad N→128), 8 k-steps | 64×96 | smem | N=99 odd, padded; M=B large; **~45–60%** 🟡 |
210	| **bwd dX** (per linear) dX = dY·W | 18,816 | K_in | N_out | mirror of fwd, swap N↔K | 128×128 | acts HBM | same class as the fwd it mirrors |
211	| **bwd dW** (per linear) dW = dYᵀ·X | N_out | K_in | **T=18,816** | **m64nNk16 contracting full T**, T/16=**1176 k-steps** | dW output tile (e.g. 64×128 for ff0_w[512,128]) | **dY,X stream from HBM acts** | **K=T huge → the most TC-efficient GEMMs; ~80–88%** 🟡 |
212	
213	**Why dW is the TC-friendliest and how Q2 lands here.** dW = Σ_{t∈[0,T)} dY[t,:]ᵀ
214	X[t,:]. In GEMM terms (M_g=N_out, N_g=K_in, **K_g=T**) the contraction is the full
215	token dimension. **Each CTA owns a fixed (M_g×N_g) output tile of dW and contracts
216	ALL T tokens itself** by streaming dY[*, n_out_tile] and X[*, k_in_tile] from the
217	HBM acts buffer in **fixed ascending-t k-step order**. No `[nCTA×total]` partial,
218	no cross-CTA reduce — the dW tile is written **once**, complete. This is the literal
219	Q2 deliverable.
220	
221	- **Tile ownership map.** dW tensors are small (largest decoder weight = ff0_w/ff2_w
222	  = 512×128 = 65,536 elems = 8 output-tiles of 64×128). The 30 weight tensors yield
223	  ~**O(60) dW output tiles** total. Assign tiles to CTAs round-robin by a fixed
224	  `tile_id = atomic-free static partition` (tile_id → CTA = tile_id % nCTA), so
225	  every step the same CTA owns the same tile (determinism + L2 warmth). With ~60
226	  tiles and 132 SMs, ~half the SMs own a dW tile; **the rest are NOT idle** — they
227	  own dX tiles and the fwd GEMMs in P1 (the phases overlap within P1; dW and dX of
228	  a layer are independent given dY).
229	- **Determinism.** k-order is **ascending t**, fixed and identical on every run;
230	  one CTA owns each tile end-to-end (no work-steal split of a tile's K-loop). No
231	  float atomics. ✔ matches the owner's determinism rule.
232	- **Eliminated traffic (quantified).** Removes the 223 MB partial buffer and its
233	  446 MB/step round-trip (**133 µs**); adds ~39 MB/step acts (**11.5 µs**). Net
234	  **−122 µs/step** of HBM time on the decoder.
235	
236	**What remains of P2 (the embedding scatter).** tok/pos grads are index-scatter,
237	not a GEMM: `g.tok[token_id·d + j] += dh` and `g.pos[s·d + j] += dh`
238	(`model_stages_decoder.cuh:981-988`). These collide across tokens/CTAs and **cannot
239	be output-stationary** (the output row depends on data-dependent `token_id`).
240	**Deterministic owner map (Q2 tail):**
241	  - **tok** (99 rows × 128): owner = `row j of tok-tensor → CTA (row % nCTA)`. Each
242	    owner CTA, after B0, loops **all T tokens in ascending t**, and for each token
243	    whose id maps to a row it owns, accumulates `dh[t,:]`. Fixed t-order + single
244	    owner per row ⇒ deterministic, atomic-free. Cost: each CTA scans T token-ids
245	    (cheap, T=18,816 int reads, ~75 KB) — but only accumulates for its rows.
246	  - **pos** (4 rows × 128): trivially 4 owner-CTAs, each sums dh[t, s_owned] over
247	    its tokens. (mamba pos=8, vit pos=17 — same pattern.)
248	  - This is the ONLY surviving cross-CTA accumulation; it needs **P0 zero + B0**
249	    (the embedding accumulators) and is folded into P1's tail (no extra barrier).
250	
251	### 3.2 ViT (d=128, dff=512, kSeq=17, kNPatch=16, kPatch=49, V=97)
252	
253	Same six GEMM families as decoder, **M-rows = T = B·kSeq = 4704·17 = 79,968**
254	(every position contributes — head uses CLS pos 0 only, M=B). Attention is **FULL
255	(no causal mask)** (`model_stage_vit.cuh:346`), so scores/ctx are S=17 square — still
256	too small for wgmma (17×17×32), kept scalar. **Extra GEMM: patch_proj** (per-patch
257	embed, Linear(49→128)) — M=B·16=75,264, N=128, K=49 → m64n128k16 with K=49 padded
258	to 64, 4 k-steps; low roof (~40–55% 🟡, short K, odd pad) but small FLOP share.
259	
260	ViT dW for ff0_w/ff2_w (512×128) contracts T=79,968 (T/16 = **4,998 k-steps**) —
261	even more TC-efficient than decoder (**~82–88%** 🟡). ViT FLOPs/step ≈ decoder ×
262	(79,968/18,816) on the per-position GEMMs ≈ **~190 GFLOP/step** 🟡 (rough; head and
263	patch_proj differ) ⇒ bf16 floor ≈ **~190 µs**. ViT is the most TC-bound of the
264	three and benefits most from R2.

266	### 3.3 Mamba (d=128, d_inner=256, state=16, dt_rank=8, kSeq=8, V=97) — §8
267	
268	Projection GEMMs (in_proj 128→512, x_proj 256→40, dt_proj 8→256, out_proj 256→128),
269	M-rows = T = B·8 = 37,632. These ARE wgmma-able (in_proj K=128, out_proj K=256).
270	**But the selective scan (the core) is NOT a GEMM** — it is a sequential recurrence
271	over seq=8 per channel, held in registers (`mb_scan_fwd:487`). §8 shows mamba is
272	**memory-roof-bound**, so TC on the projections is a secondary win; the primary
273	mamba wins are bf16 storage + Q2 + tiling the proj GEMMs around the register scan.

358	## 5. bf16 policy (the dtype boundary table) + parity gate
359	
360	### 5.1 Op-level dtype boundary (matches torch autocast)
361	
362	The owner's rule: bf16 storage + matmuls, **fp32 accumulators**, and autocast keeps
363	softmax/LN/CE/optimizer math fp32. Exact table:
364	
365	| op | inputs | compute | output stored | rationale |
366	|---|---|---|---|---|
367	| in_proj / out_proj / ff0 / ff2 / head / patch_proj (and all dX/dW) | **bf16** | wgmma, **fp32 acc** | bf16 acts / **fp32 grad** | autocast matmul boundary; grad stays fp32 for the optimizer |
368	| attention scores / softmax | bf16 q,k | **fp32** (dot + softmax) | bf16 weights | autocast keeps softmax fp32; tiny S so cost negligible |
369	| LayerNorm (fwd+bwd) | bf16 x | **fp32** (mean/var/normalize) | bf16 y; **fp32 xhat/inv cached** | autocast LN fp32; the two mean-correction terms need fp32 |
370	| GELU / SiLU / softplus | bf16 | **fp32** transcendental | bf16 | autocast elementwise upcast; exact-erf GELU (`dec_gelu:99`) |
371	| cross-entropy / NLL | fp32 logits | **fp32** (logsumexp), **fp64** loss reduce | fp32 grad | the 1e-5 loss rel-tol is the tightest gate (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:171`) |
372	| selective scan (mamba) | bf16 x_main, B, C | **fp32 scan state in registers** | bf16 y_scan | scan is memory-bound; fp32 state preserves the recurrence (`mb_scan_fwd:492`) |
373	| optimizer apply (all 11 tails) | fp32 grad + fp32 state | **fp32** | fp32 params + state | autocast never touches the optimizer; FusedOptState is fp32 |
374	
375	**Storage halving (the §4.3 budgets):** every `[kSeq×width]` smem activation array
376	in `DecSampleSmem` / `VitSampleSmem` / `MambaSampleSmem` becomes `__nv_bfloat16`;
377	the **LN caches (xhat, inv_std) and the fp32 reduction scratch `red[256]` stay
378	fp32** (they feed fp32 LN bwd). Decoder ~42→~21 KB, vit ~188→~94 KB, mamba ~145→~73
379	KB (computed in §4.3). New per-model smem budgets are the "+ bf16 halving" column.
380	
381	### 5.2 Parity gate (chaos-floor methodology — read the calibrated-gate comments)
382	
383	The existing gate (`tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py`) is explicit that an
384	**L3 loss-trajectory-vs-eager test is ill-posed** for the surrogate path (:8-16) and
385	that the faithful unit is the optimizer tail + a **grok smoke floor** (:27-31). For
386	the **real** TC cells the bf16 gate is therefore **tiered**, matching the L3-REAL
387	decoder gate at `:288-294`:
388	
389	1. **Single-step grad parity vs eager bf16-autocast** (NOT fp32 eager): build the
390	   eager model under `torch.autocast(bf16)`, one fwd+bwd, compare every weight grad.
391	   **Tolerance: rel ≤ 2e-2** 🟡 (bf16 has ~3 mantissa bits; this is the autocast
392	   round-off class, far looser than the fp32 gate's `1e-4` at `:292`). Loss rel ≤
393	   `1e-3` (logsumexp is fp32 so it stays tight).
394	2. **Determinism A/B/A:** run the cell 3× (A, B, A); assert run A == run A
395	   **bit-identically** (fixed tile ownership + fixed k-order + no float atomics
396	   guarantee it). B may differ from A only if B perturbs scheduling — it must not,
397	   so A==B==A bit-exact. This is the real witness that §3's determinism holds.
398	3. **Grok-floor (the chaos-robust gate):** 3 seeds, real model + the bf16-TC fused
399	   train step, must reach the grokking accuracy threshold (mirrors `:294` "must
400	   grok"). Because bf16 + reordered fp32 reductions make the **loss trajectory**
401	   chaotically diverge from eager (sensitive dependence — the calibrated-gate point
402	   at `:12-16`), the final-accuracy floor — not the trajectory — is the correct
403	   acceptance criterion for the bf16 cells.
404	
405	> 🟡 The 2e-2 grad tolerance is my estimate from the bf16 mantissa width; the build
406	> agent must **calibrate it against an eager-bf16 oracle** the same way the fp32
407	> gate was calibrated against fp64 (`:349-364`), and tighten if the oracle is closer.

412	
413	R1 stays inside the **current scalar design**, lands in days, and **every R1 piece is
414	reused wholesale by R2**:
415	
416	| R1 win | mechanism | expected multiplier | reused by R2? |
417	|---|---|---|---|
418	| **k-samples-per-CTA** (vs one-sample-at-a-time) | process K_samp rows per CTA inner loop, unroll the owner-computes GEMM loops over K_samp → ILP + register reuse of weights | **~3–6×** 🟡 (the current `dec_linear` does 1 row's dot at a time with zero cross-row reuse; batching K_samp amortizes the weight loads and fills the pipeline) | yes — becomes the M_tile of §3 |
419	| **split-K dW without TC** | the Q2 output-stationary dW (§3.1) but with scalar fp32 contraction over full T | **kills the 223 MB partials → −133 µs** | yes — same ownership map, just swap the inner loop for wgmma |

423	- R1's split-K dW and bf16 storage are **prerequisites R2 needs anyway** (the
424	  ownership map, the dtype boundary, the halved smem that makes vit placeable). Doing
425	  them in the scalar design **de-risks them independently** of the hard wgmma
426	  descriptor work.
427	- The integration agent currently landing vit/mamba cells builds on the **current**
428	  design; R1 is **incremental** on that (k-samples + split-K + bf16 are localized
429	  edits to the existing `*_linear` / dW loops and the phase structure), whereas R2 is
430	  a GEMM-engine rewrite. R1 churn is low and additive; an R2-first rewrite would

433	  practice" to **single-digit× the bf16 floor** (split-K removes the 3× partials

438	**Do not skip R1.** The only R1 piece R2 *replaces* is the scalar inner dot (→

443	## 7. Sort / SG2 (in-CTA bitonic sort + sequence-space partitioning)
444	
445	### 7.1 In-CTA bitonic sort (eliminate the host round-trip)
446	
447	SG2 currently sorts each tensor's flat grad by **|grad| ascending** on the **host**
448	(`torch.sort`, `opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:34-42`) and feeds `perm`/`unsort` into the
449	kernel. **Design: a STAGE -1 in-CTA bitonic sort** so the whole step is launch-free.
450	- Each CTA owns a whole tensor (tensor-per-CTA, `opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:64-66`),
451	  so the sort is **per-CTA over that tensor's N keys** — no cross-tensor crossing
452	  (the exact correctness hazard the header flags at :38-42).
453	- **Bitonic sorting network** — the standard nested form: outer `k` doubles 2→N
454	  (`ceil(log2 N)` levels), inner `j` halves k→1, giving **~½·(log₂N)²
455	  compare-exchange passes** total (N=512 → ~45 passes, N=65,536 → ~136 — NOT
456	  log₂N), each pass `__syncthreads`-separated over N/2 pairs (threads stride). Keys =
457	  `|grad[i]|` (fp32), payload = original index i → produces `perm`; `unsort` is the
458	  inverse scatter.
459	- **Determinism:** bitonic is a **fixed comparison network** (data-independent
460	  schedule) → deterministic. Ties: break by **ascending original index** (stable),
461	  matching the host sort's stable-sort contract. No atomics.
462	- **Cost/feasibility:** largest race param ~65,536 elems → ~136 compare-exchange
463	  passes × ~33K compares/pass = trivial vs the CSA/HCA attention that follows (still
464	  O(N·passes) ≪ the dense HCA's O(N·Nh·heads·head_dim)). Keys fit a per-CTA smem
465	  scratch (65,536×4 = 256 KB — **too large for one CTA's smem**); so for N > ~8192
466	  the sort is **global-memory bitonic** (compare-exchange in the tensor's HBM slice,
467	  `__syncthreads` per stage) — still launch-free, just not smem-resident. 🟡 For the
468	  race's small tensors (most are ≤512) the smem path applies. Drop-in as STAGE -1;
469	  the header is already written to accept it (`opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:55-57`).
470	
471	### 7.2 Sequence-space partitioning of the SG2 meta-net (replace tensor-per-CTA)
472	
473	The current SG2 stage is **tensor-per-CTA** (one CTA does a whole tensor's
474	CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU), a conscious correctness-first divergence from design-req-#1
475	(`opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:97-119`) whose **cost** is owned: with ~30 tensors and
476	~132 SMs, ~100 CTAs pull an empty queue and idle, and one 256-thread CTA does each
477	tensor's entire (dense) HCA attention serially.
478	
479	**Design: sequence-space partitioning for the LARGE tensors.** The stage bodies
480	**already take explicit N/Nc/Nh and use CTA-cooperative grid-stride loops** (the
481	header author built for this — `:117-119`), so **only the outer driver changes**:
482	- For a large tensor, spread its N rows across **a cluster of CTAs** (or the whole
483	  grid for the single largest), with **one grid barrier after the compress stage**
484	  (so all compressed K/V are visible before attention/topk read them — the genuine
485	  cross-CTA coupling the header names at :100-104).
486	- Small tensors (which dominate the race's param *count*) stay **tensor-per-CTA**
487	  (one CTA, barrier-light) — a size threshold `SG_TUNED_SG2_SEQPART_MIN` routes.
488	- **Determinism preserved:** the compress/attention reductions are still
489	  owner-computes per output element in fixed order; the grid barrier only orders
490	  visibility, not summation order.
491	- This reuses the **same stage bodies** verbatim — the change is the row-ownership
492	  in the driver + one barrier, exactly the refactor the header was written to admit.
493

496	## 8. Mamba scan — confirm memory-roof-bound, design only what helps
497	
498	**Arithmetic intensity of the scan (computed reasoning).** Per (sample, channel j),
499	the scan does, over seq=8 and state=16: ~8×16 FMAs for h-update + 8×16 for y-accum
500	≈ **256 MAC = 512 FLOP/channel**. It reads x_main[8], dt_pre[8], Bmat[8×16],
501	Cmat[8×16], A_log[16] ≈ (8+8+128+128+16) bf16 = 288×2 = **576 B/channel**, writes
502	y_scan[8] = 16 B. AI ≈ 512 FLOP / 592 B ≈ **0.86 FLOP/B**. The roofline ridge for
503	bf16-TC is 989.4e12/3.35e12 ≈ **295 FLOP/B**. **0.86 ≪ 295 → the scan is deeply
504	memory-roof-bound** (by ~340×). This confirms the briefing and the header's own
505	"memory-roof-bound" framing.
506	
507	**Therefore for mamba:**
508	- **Do NOT** try to TC the scan (it is not a GEMM and is memory-bound anyway).
509	- **Keep fp32 scan state in registers** (`mb_scan_fwd:492` `h[kState]`,
510	  `mb_scan_bwd` `hh[kSeq+1][kState]`) — the seq=8 register exploit is correct and is
511	  what keeps smem off the 128 KB the naive h-in-smem would need (`model_stage_mamba3.cuh:74-88`).
512	- **bf16 storage** for the scan's inputs/outputs (x_main, B, C, y_scan) — halves the
513	  576 B/channel traffic → the direct multiplier on the memory-bound scan.
514	- **TC the projection GEMMs around the scan** (in_proj 128→512, out_proj 256→128,
515	  x_proj 256→40) — these ARE GEMMs (§3.3), M-rows=T=37,632, and tiling them with
516	  wgmma + Fork-B dW is the real mamba compute win. The scan sits between them as a
517	  register-resident barrier-free stage.
518	- **conv1d** (depthwise k=3, `mb_conv1d_fwd:420`) is also memory-bound (3 MACs/elem)
519	  → bf16 storage, kept scalar.
520	
521	Net mamba story: **Q5 (bf16) + Q2 (split-K dW) + tiled proj GEMMs**; the scan itself
522	is left as the proven register recurrence, only its operands go bf16.

548	**Absent definitions yield a correct untuned kernel** (contract rule 3,
549	`COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md:28-31`): default M_tile=128, depth=2, etc. all compose into
550	a valid cell. **Do not touch the Optuna optimizer-hyperparameter tuner in `tuning/`**
551	— that is a separate system (the briefing and `AUTOTUNE_LINKAGE.md` both stress this;
552	this is the **kernel** autotuner).
553	
554	---
555	
556	## 10. Validation + measurement plan
557	
558	### 10.1 Per-phase gates
559	
560	| phase | gate |
561	|---|---|
562	| R1 split-K dW (scalar) | grad parity vs current cell **bit-identical** (same fp32 math, just output-stationary; ascending-t order matches the old ascending-CTA reduce *only if* both sum T in the same order — verify, the order changed from CTA-major to t-major so it is fp32-rel ≤ 1e-5, **not** bit-exact) 🟡 |
563	| R1 bf16 storage | grad parity vs eager-bf16, rel ≤ 2e-2 (§5.2); grok-floor 3 seeds |
564	| R2 wgmma per GEMM | **SASS audit** (§10.3) + single-step grad parity vs eager-bf16 |
565	| R2 full cell | determinism A/B/A bit-exact; grok-floor 3 seeds; occupancy-refuse test (force a too-large smem config, assert `cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources`, **no hang**) |
566	| recomposition (every phase) | all 33 cells regenerate from `megakernel_codegen.py`; `git diff` generator-consistent (`COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md:5,37`); out-of-tree portability TU compiles (rule 4) |
567	
568	### 10.2 Roofline protocol per cell (the owner's metric)
569	
570	Reuse `tuning/roofline.py`'s **timed-FLOPs methodology** (ncu blocked —
571	ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM, `roofline.py:5`): achieved = FLOPs_per_step / wall_per_step;
572	wall = CUDA-synced over 100 steps after 25 warmup, **quiet-GPU window** (no other
573	process — the 3 grok-smoke + tuner fleet must be idle for the measurement window).
574	Ceiling = min(bf16_tc_peak, AI·HBM_BW); fraction = achieved/ceiling. **Per-pipeline
575	precision = bf16** now (the cells compute bf16), so the ceiling is the **989.4 TF/s
576	BF16 line** (`roofline.py:287`, `_PRECISION_PEAK['bf16']`), not tf32.
577	
578	### 10.3 SASS audit checklist (per cell .so)
579	
580	`cuobjdump -sass <mega_model_opt>.o | grep -E ...`:
581	- ✔ `WGMMA` present (the in-kernel tensor-core MMA — absence = scalar fallback shipped).
582	- ✔ `wgmma.wait_group` / `wgmma.commit_group` present (pipeline correctness).
583	- ✔ cp.async (`LDGSTS`) present (phase-1 staging) / `UTMALDG` (phase-2 TMA).
584	- ✔ `setmaxnreg` (`R2UR`/the warpgroup reg ops) present (producer/consumer split).
585	- ✔ **no `STL`/`LDL` spills** in the consumer wgmma loop (register pressure check;
586	  the `--maxrregcount` tuned dim exists to fix this if it appears).
587	
588	### 10.4 Step-time budget table (projection; decoder, bf16)
589	
590	| component | µs (projected) | basis |
591	|---|---|---|
592	| fwd+bwd GEMMs (TC) | ~60–90 µs 🟡 | 45 µs bf16 floor ÷ ~0.5–0.75 achievable roof (§3 per-GEMM classes, occ=1) |
593	| acts HBM round-trip (Fork B) | ~11.5 µs | 39 MB / 3.35 TB/s (computed §1.3) |
594	| grid barriers (2, Fork B) | ~2–4 µs 🟡 | 2 × ~1–2 µs (`__nanosleep` backoff rendezvous, no co-residency stall at occ=1) |
595	| elementwise (LN/GELU/softmax/CE, fp32) | ~10–20 µs 🟡 | small S; dominated by the 99-wide CE logsumexp × B |
596	| optimizer tail (fused, adamw) | ~5–8 µs 🟡 | 422,755 elems × (read g + r/w m,v + w param) ≈ 8.5 MB / 3.35 TB/s ≈ 2.5 µs + overhead |
597	| **total / step** | **~90–135 µs** 🟡 | → **~7,500–11,000 steps/s** |
598	| **roofline fraction** | **~35–50%** 🟡 | achieved (45 GFLOP / ~110 µs ≈ 410 GF/s) / 989 TF/s — memory-bound, so read against AI·BW: at AI≈45GFLOP/50MB≈900 FLOP/B the cell is **compute-bound** and the fraction is GEMM-roof-limited ~0.5 |
599	
600	> 🟡 The whole budget is a **no-silicon projection** (no GPU runs permitted here; the
601	> 3 grok-smoke + tuner processes are live). The achievable-roof column is the honest
602	> uncertainty: short-K GEMMs at occ=1 will not hit peak. The build agent measures
603	> the real numbers via §10.2 and the SASS audit confirms the instructions are
604	> present.
605	
606	---
607	
608	## 11. Effort / sequencing (day-level; substrate vs per-header)
609	
610	| phase | work | substrate vs header | recompose+validate | days 🟡 |
611	|---|---|---|---|---|
612	| **R1.1** | k-samples-per-CTA in `dec_/vit_/mb_linear` + dW loops | per-header (3 model headers) | regen 33 cells, parity + grok-floor | 1–2 |
613	| **R1.2** | split-K output-stationary dW (kills partials) + embedding owner-map | per-header (3) + phase struct in 3 `fused_*_megakernel.cuh` | bit/rel grad parity, drop B1 phase | 2 |
614	| **R1.3** | bf16 scalar storage (§5 dtype table) | per-header (3 SampleSmem structs) | eager-bf16 parity (calibrate tol), re-check smem budgets | 1–2 |
615	| **R2.1** | new `wgmma.cuh` substrate (ss-wgmma PTX + smem descriptors) + SASS verify on a microbench | **substrate** (1 new header) | SASS audit (WGMMA present) | 3–5 (the hard part) |
616	| **R2.2** | producer/consumer pipeline (mbarrier ring + cp.async staging) in a shared GEMM helper | **substrate** (extend `wgs::`) | per-GEMM grad parity | 2–3 |
617	| **R2.3** | wire wgmma GEMMs into the 3 model headers (replace scalar dots; keep scores/ctx/scan scalar) | per-header (3) | full-cell parity + determinism A/B/A + roofline | 2–3 |
618	| **R2.4** | TMA (host descriptors + `cp.async.bulk.tensor`) — phase-2 optional | substrate + autotuner dims | SASS (UTMALDG), roofline delta | 2–3 |
619	| **R2.5** | SG2 in-CTA bitonic sort (STAGE -1) + sequence-space partition driver | per-header (`opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh` driver) | SG2 parity (1e-5) + determinism | 2–3 |
620	| **autotuner** | add 7 `SG_TUNED_*` to `_tuned_inject.py` MACROS + pass | tooling | `tuning/test_build_injection` | 1 |
621	
622	**Substrate work** (inherited by all 33 cells): `wgmma.cuh`, the `wgs::` pipeline
623	extension, the TMA descriptors, the new autotuner macros. **Per-header work** (lands
624	once per model, recomposed across all 11 optimizers): the k-samples / split-K / bf16
625	edits and the wgmma wiring in the 3 `model_stage_*.cuh` + 3 `fused_*_megakernel.cuh`.
626	**Optimizer headers** are largely untouched except §4's epilogue-fusion (§ below).
627	
628	**Recomposition cost per phase** is one `megakernel_codegen.py` run + the parity
629	suite + a quiet-window roofline pass; it is dominated by the **per-cell CUTLASS-free
630	nvcc compile** (the cells are header-only; no CUTLASS in the L3 path, so the heavy
631	`mma.cuh` TUs are NOT rebuilt). Heavy-TU serial-compile OOM (`mma.cuh:384-396`) does
632	**not** apply to the L3 cells — another reason the in-kernel wgmma path is preferred
633	over dragging CUTLASS device-side.
634	
635	---
636	
637	## Appendix A — Optimizer epilogue-fusion verdict table (Q3)
638	
639	The dW tile is **register-resident** at the end of P1's dW GEMM (the fp32
640	accumulator fragment). An optimizer whose apply is **element-local** can run **in
641	that epilogue**, before the fragment is stored — eliminating B1+P2 (the grad never
642	leaves registers for those tails). Verdict per the 11 (apply math is
643	`opt_components.cuh:184-254`):
644	
645	| optimizer | element-local apply? | epilogue-fusable? | what it needs before apply | fallback if not fused |
646	|---|---|---|---|---|
647	| **AdamW** | yes (m,v,param all element-local, `adamw_step`) | **✔ FUSE** | bc1/bc2 (host scalars) | — |
648	| **Lion** | yes (`lion_step`, m only) | **✔ FUSE** | — | — |
649	| **Grokfast** | yes (EMA fused in apply, `opt_stages_precompute.cuh:52`) | **✔ FUSE** | — | — |
650	| **GrokAdamW** | yes (EMA fused, `:53`) | **✔ FUSE** | — | — |
651	| **NeuralGrok** | yes (psi MLP inline, `opt_components.cuh:222-229`) | **✔ FUSE** | psi-net weights (per-tensor, in `extra`) | — |
652	| **Prodigy** | apply is element-local BUT needs **global d** first | **✗ stage** | `d_factor` = cross-ALL-tensors r/s reduce (`opt_stages_precompute.cuh:58`) | precompute-d phase (B) **before** P2; order: P1 dW → B → d-reduce → B → apply |
653	| **Muon** | NO — needs Newton–Schulz on the **full matrix** | **✗ NOT fusable** | NS orth direction (5 matmul iters, `:59`) | keep staged: P1 dW → B → NS phase → B → apply (`muon_update_step`) |
654	| **SuperGrok11** | apply element-local; needs **per-tensor gate** | **✗ stage (light)** | one per-tensor cosine reduction (`:60`, single-drain, no grid barrier) | per-tensor mu+gate stage before apply (CTA-local, barrier-free) |
655	| **SuperGrok15** | apply element-local; gate is a **host scalar** | **partial** — mu is element-local, gate host-set | mu meta-MLP forward (`:62`); gate via `FusedScalars.gate` | mu stage before apply (gate already a scalar → no reduce) |
656	| **SuperGrok2** | apply is Adam on `smart_grad` | **✗ separate tail** | the whole CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net (§7) produces `smart_grad` | the SG2 in-kernel meta stages (own phase), then Adam apply |
657	
658	**Summary:** **5 of 11 fully epilogue-fusable** (adamw/lion/grokfast/grokadamw/
659	neuralgrok → 2 phases / 1 barrier). Prodigy/SG11/SG15 need **one reduction phase
660	before apply** (3 phases / 2 barriers). **Muon and SG2 are NOT fusable** — they keep
661	their multi-phase staged structure (NS orthogonalization / meta-net), which is
662	correct and faithful to the per-op pipelines (`opt_components.cuh:19-27`). The
663	fusion is a per-optimizer codegen branch in the cell template — it lands in
664	`fused_megakernel.cuh`'s phase selection, inherited by all model×opt combos.
665	
666	## Appendix B — What is explicitly NOT done (road not taken)
667	
668	- **Host-CUTLASS GEMMs (`mma.cuh`) for the L3 cells: REJECTED.** CUTLASS collectives
669	  are not device-callable (own their TMA mainloop, `mma.cuh:145-153`), and ~15–30
670	  host launches/step **without CUDA graphs** is pure launch overhead that swamps the
671	  45 µs compute floor. The owner forbids graphs and mandates one persistent kernel.
672	  ∴ in-kernel wgmma is the only consistent path. (`mma.cuh` stays for the L1 per-op
673	  Muon/SG2 paths it already serves.)
674	- **Global per-layer grid barrier (the briefing's literal Q1 phrasing): REJECTED** —
675	  it serializes the grid L×#GEMMs/step. Fork B keeps fwd→bwd CTA-local.
676	- **DSMEM cluster reduce for dW: NOT USED** — Fork B has no dW reduce.
677	- **TF32 path: NOT the race precision** — bf16 is (owner decision); TF32 stays only
678	  as the `mma.cuh` fp32-accuracy fallback for L1.
679	- **FP8: out of scope** — not in the owner's precision decision; the roofline tracks
680	  it only as a drawn ceiling (`roofline.py:51`).
681

2	// csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/wgmma.cuh
3	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4	// R2 TENSOR-CORE SUBSTRATE — hand-rolled in-kernel ss-wgmma for Hopper sm_90a.
5	//
6	// Implements DESIGN-TC-PIPELINE.md §4.1 item 1 + item 2: the in-kernel
7	// `wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64nNk16.f32.bf16.bf16` warp-group MMA with
8	// smem-resident A AND B operands ("ss" = shared-shared), the 64-bit smem
9	// core-matrix descriptors those operands require, the fp32 accumulator
10	// fragment management, swizzle-mode handling, and the
11	// wgmma.fence / wgmma.commit_group / wgmma.wait_group choreography.
12	//
13	// This is the hand-written, correctness-gated GEMM-engine layer the three
14	// model-stage headers (decoder / vit / mamba3) build their tiled fwd/bwd
15	// pipelines on (DESIGN §3). It does NOT include or depend on CUTLASS
16	// (mma.cuh): host-launched CUTLASS collectives are not device-callable and
17	// are explicitly REJECTED for the L3 persistent-megakernel path
18	// (DESIGN Appendix B). This header is the only WGMMA path inside the kernel.
19	//
20	// PORTABILITY (COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md rules 1-4): header-only, self-contained,
21	// substrate + CUDA only. It includes ONLY <cuda_bf16.h> / <cuda_runtime.h> /
22	// <cstdint>; a third project lifts THIS file (+ warp_specialize.cuh /
23	// primitives.cuh for the pipeline) and instantiates the wrappers with no other
24	// repo dependency. All arch-specific PTX is guarded on __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900;
25	// pre-sm_90 / gfx942 compile to the documented scalar fallback so the codegen
26	// matrix still builds (the model headers keep their scalar `*_linear` there).
27	//
28	// MAXIMAL-PTX DISCIPLINE: every inline-asm sequence cites the PTX ISA section
29	// (CUDA 12.4 / PTX ISA 8.4) it implements. The PTX is the point.
30	//
31	// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
32	//  API CONTRACT — what a model-stage header author calls (integration seam)
33	// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
34	//
35	// The next phase (R2.3, wiring wgmma into model_stage_{decoder,vit,mamba3})
36	// consumes EXACTLY the following. All symbols live in `sg::sm90::wgs::`
37	// (the same namespace as warp_specialize.cuh's Mbarrier / setmaxnreg helpers —
38	// this header REOPENS that namespace, it does not fork a new one).
39	//
40	// --- 1. The accumulator fragment ------------------------------------------
41	//   template <int N> struct WgmmaAccum;
42	//     Per-thread fp32 accumulator for an m64×N output tile. Holds N/2 floats
43	//     in registers (NOT smem). One object per consumer thread; the 128
44	//     warpgroup threads together hold the full 64×N tile. Layout is the
45	//     PTX ISA "Figure 149 / register fragment for .f32 accumulators"
46	//     (§<ip>.3) mapping — see frag_row()/frag_col() below for the exact
47	//     thread→(row,col) decode the epilogue uses to store results.
48	//       .zero()                 — clear all N/2 lanes to 0.0f (call before the
49	//                                 first accumulating wgmma if scaleD=accumulate).
50	//       .c[i]                   — the i-th fp32 register (i in [0, N/2)).
51	//
52	// --- 2. The smem matrix descriptor ----------------------------------------
53	//   struct SmemDesc { uint64_t desc; };
54	//   __device__ SmemDesc make_smem_desc<Swizzle>(const void* smem_base,
55	//                                                uint32_t lbo, uint32_t sbo);
56	//     Packs the 64-bit shared-memory descriptor (PTX ISA §<ip>.4,
57	//     "Shared memory matrix descriptor"). `smem_base` is a generic smem
58	//     pointer to the (0,0) element of the operand's core-matrix tile; lbo /
59	//     sbo are the leading- / stride-byte-offsets in BYTES (the helper applies
60	//     the mandated >>4 encoding). `Swizzle` selects the swizzle mode.
61	//     Convenience builders for the canonical bf16 Major-K tile layouts (the
62	//     operand's MN extent is a compile-time template arg; the tile MUST be
63	//     staged in the canonical Major-K core-matrix layout — see the builders):
64	//       make_desc_A_kmajor<M=64, Swizzle>(smem)  — A operand (M rows × K=16)
65	//       make_desc_B_kmajor<N,    Swizzle>(smem)  — B operand (N rows × K=16)
66	//
67	// --- 3. The MMA + choreography --------------------------------------------
68	//   __device__ void wgmma_fence();                         // §<ip>.2
69	//   __device__ void wgmma_commit_group();                  // §<ip>.5
70	//   template <int N> __device__ void wgmma_wait_group();   // §<ip>.6
71	//
72	//   template <int N, int ScaleD, int TransA, int TransB>
73	//   __device__ void wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16(WgmmaAccum<N>& acc,
74	//                                       SmemDesc descA, SmemDesc descB);
75	//     One m64×N×16 ss-wgmma issue (PTX ISA §<ip>.1). ScaleD=0 OVERWRITES
76	//     the accumulator (D = A·B); ScaleD=1 ACCUMULATES (D += A·B). TransA/TransB
77	//     select operand transpose (the .trans descriptor bit). N must be one of
78	//     the legal bf16 shapes {8,16,32,64,96,128,256}; the design selects 128
79	//     (in/out/ff GEMMs), 96 (decoder head V=99 padded), 64 (ragged).
80	//
81	//   Full mainloop helper (the choreography in one call — what the model
82	//   headers actually invoke for a K-tile chain):
83	//   template <int N, int TransA, int TransB, typename DescGen>
84	//   __device__ void wgmma_mainloop_kchain(WgmmaAccum<N>& acc, int k_steps,
85	//                                         DescGen gen);
86	//     Runs `k_steps` ss-wgmma issues in FIXED ASCENDING k-order (DESIGN §3.1
87	//     determinism rule), first issue ScaleD=0 then accumulate, with one
88	//     fence before the group and one commit+wait_group<0> after. `gen(k)`
89	//     returns the {descA, descB} pair for k-step k (the caller advances the
90	//     smem pointer / pipeline stage). Bit-identical regardless of how the
91	//     caller stages the operands (cp.async vs pre-loaded), which is what gate
92	//     (c) (pipelined == unpipelined) verifies.
93	//
94	// --- 4. Tunable template parameters (DESIGN §9, SG_TUNED_* names) ----------
95	//   SG_TUNED_TILE_N   — wgmma N (output tile width). Default 128. {64,128,256}.
96	//                       The `N` template arg above is bound to this by callers.
97	//   SG_TUNED_TILE_M   — token-tile rows per CTA (the M-tile). Default 128.
98	//                       wgmma M is fixed at 64 (the atom); TILE_M/64 = number
99	//                       of stacked atoms a CTA's consumer warpgroup issues.
100	//   (SG_TUNED_PIPE_DEPTH / SG_TUNED_WG_COUNT belong to tile_pipeline.cuh.)

103	// --- 5. smem layout + alignment requirements (cite: PTX ISA) --------------
104	//   * Operand smem tiles MUST be 16-byte aligned. The matrix descriptor's
105	//     start-address field is the smem byte address >>4 (PTX ISA §<ip>.4),
106	//     so the low 4 bits MUST be zero — a non-16B-aligned tile silently drops
107	//     them and reads the wrong matrix. Allocate operand smem as
108	//     `__align__(16)` (or via an aligned smem arena).

112	//     multiple of 128 and the issuing warpgroup must be convergent.

118	//     (rows×cols, "8 rows of 16 cols", 128-bit) core matrices; the K-tile is
119	//     16 (the atom's k). The B (RHS) tile for an N-wide output is N×16 bf16.
120	//
121	// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
122	#include <cuda_bf16.h>
123	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
124	#include <cstdint>
125	
126	namespace sg { namespace sm90 { namespace wgs {
127	
128	// =========================================================================
129	//  Tunable defaults (DESIGN §9). #ifndef so an out-of-tree lift / an untuned
130	//  build composes a correct kernel (CONTRACT rule 3). The kernel-autotuner
131	//  injects -DSG_TUNED_* per-TU; absent, these defaults apply.
132	// =========================================================================
133	#ifndef SG_TUNED_TILE_N
134	#define SG_TUNED_TILE_N 128
135	#endif
136	#ifndef SG_TUNED_TILE_M
137	#define SG_TUNED_TILE_M 128
138	#endif

140	// wgmma atom M is FIXED by the ISA (m64nNk16 → M=64); the CTA's M-tile is
141	// SG_TUNED_TILE_M, issued as SG_TUNED_TILE_M/64 stacked atoms.
142	static constexpr int kWgmmaAtomM = 64;
143	static constexpr int kWgmmaAtomK = 16;   // bf16 atom K (m64nNk16)
144	
145	// =========================================================================
146	//  Swizzle mode (PTX ISA §<ip>.4, descriptor bits 62-61 "swizzle mode").
147	//
148	//  The shared-memory matrix descriptor encodes how the 128-bit core-matrix
149	//  rows are interleaved in smem to avoid bank conflicts on the wgmma read.
150	//  CRITICAL: the descriptor's layout_type field (bits 63:62) does NOT use a
151	//  size-ascending encoding. The hardware/CUTLASS encoding is
152	//  (cute/arch/mma_sm90_desc.hpp LayoutType, verified):
153	//    NONE/INTERLEAVE = 0,  SWIZZLE_128B = 1,  SWIZZLE_64B = 2,  SWIZZLE_32B = 3.
154	//  (An earlier draft had 32B=1/128B=3 swapped; the correctness path uses NONE=0
155	//  so it was unaffected, but the perf-phase swizzle modes MUST use these values.)
156	//
157	//  CORRECTNESS-PATH NOTE (deviation flagged in the report): the gated /
158	//  tested numerics path ships swizzle = NONE (kSwizzleNone). NONE is a
159	//  fully-legal descriptor mode (§<ip>.4) and is the layout the
160	//  correctness gates validate against torch. The 128B-swizzle layout is a
161	//  PERF-PHASE optimization (bank-conflict elimination on the smem read) and
162	//  is exposed here as the template parameter the model headers will select
163	//  once the quiet-GPU perf phase measures it; it is NOT required for any
164	//  correctness gate. See DESIGN §4.1 ("specify the 128-byte-swizzle layout"
165	//  is the perf target; phase-1 staging uses cp.async, §4.1 item 3).
166	// =========================================================================
167	enum SwizzleMode : uint32_t {
168	    kSwizzleNone = 0,   // INTERLEAVE / no swizzle (the correctness-path layout)
169	    kSwizzle128B = 1,   // SWIZZLE_128B
170	    kSwizzle64B  = 2,   // SWIZZLE_64B
171	    kSwizzle32B  = 3,   // SWIZZLE_32B
172	};
173	
174	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
175	//  generic-smem-pointer → matrix-descriptor start address.
176	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.4: the descriptor's bits 13-0 hold the start address of
177	//  the matrix in shared memory, encoded as the 18-bit smem byte address with
178	//  the low 4 bits dropped — i.e. addr_field = (smem_byte_addr & 0x3FFFF) >> 4.
179	//  The low 4 bits MUST be zero (16-byte alignment) or they are silently lost.
180	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
181	__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t smem_desc_encode_addr(const void* smem_ptr) {
182	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
183	    uint32_t a = static_cast<uint32_t>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(smem_ptr));
184	    return (a & 0x3FFFFu) >> 4;
185	#else
186	    (void)smem_ptr;
187	    return 0u;
188	#endif
189	}
190	
191	// =========================================================================
192	//  Shared-memory matrix descriptor (PTX ISA §<ip>.4).
193	//
194	//  64-bit layout (bit ranges per the ISA table):
195	//    bits  13: 0  start address (smem byte addr >> 4)
196	//    bits  15:14  (reserved / 0)
197	//    bits  29:16  leading-dimension byte offset (LBO) >> 4
198	//    bits  31:30  (reserved / 0)
199	//    bits  45:32  stride-dimension byte offset (SBO) >> 4
200	//    bits  48:46  (reserved / 0)
201	//    bits  51:49  matrix base offset (for swizzle; 0 for our tiles)
202	//    bits  61:52  (reserved / 0)
203	//    bits  63:62  swizzle / layout mode (0 none / 1 128B / 2 64B / 3 32B —
204	//                 the CUTLASS LayoutType encoding, see SwizzleMode above)
205	//
206	//  LBO and SBO are the byte offsets between consecutive "core matrices" along
207	//  the leading and stride dimensions respectively (§<ip>.3 "Strides").
208	//  Both are encoded >>4 (16-byte granular). The exact (LBO,SBO) depend on the
209	//  operand's smem tile layout; the make_desc_*_kmajor builders below compute
210	//  them for the canonical row-major-K bf16 tiles the model headers stage.
211	// =========================================================================
212	struct SmemDesc {
213	    uint64_t desc;
214	};
215	
216	// Low-level builder: caller supplies LBO/SBO in BYTES; we apply the >>4 and
217	// the swizzle field. Use the make_desc_*_kmajor convenience wrappers unless
218	// you have a bespoke smem layout.
219	template <SwizzleMode Swizzle = kSwizzleNone>
220	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_smem_desc(
221	    const void* smem_base, uint32_t lbo_bytes, uint32_t sbo_bytes,
222	    uint32_t base_offset = 0u
223	) {
224	    SmemDesc d;
225	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
226	    uint64_t addr = static_cast<uint64_t>(smem_desc_encode_addr(smem_base));
227	    uint64_t lbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((lbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
228	    uint64_t sbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((sbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
229	    uint64_t bo   = static_cast<uint64_t>(base_offset & 0x7u);
230	    uint64_t sw   = static_cast<uint64_t>(Swizzle & 0x3u);
231	    d.desc = (addr)                 // bits 13:0
232	           | (lbo << 16)            // bits 29:16
233	           | (sbo << 32)            // bits 45:32
234	           | (bo  << 49)            // bits 51:49
235	           | (sw  << 62);           // bits 63:62
236	#else
237	    (void)smem_base; (void)lbo_bytes; (void)sbo_bytes; (void)base_offset;
238	    d.desc = 0;
239	#endif
240	    return d;
241	}

243	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
244	//  Canonical descriptor builders for the bf16 K-major (K=16) smem operand
245	//  tiles the model headers stage (DESIGN §4.3: A tile 64×16 bf16, B tile
246	//  N×16 bf16). Major-K means the contraction dimension K is the operand's
247	//  inner GEMM dim and the wgmma reads the standard "TN" product
248	//  D[m,n] = Σ_k A[m,k]·B[n,k] with BOTH operands K-major (TransA=TransB=0).
249	//
250	//  REQUIRED smem layout (the CUTLASS-canonical Major-K INTERLEAVE layout —
251	//  ground truth, NOT a plain row-major block; see the report's "deviation"
252	//  section). For an operand of MN rows × 16 K-cols of bf16, element (mn,k) is
253	//  at the bf16 index:
254	//      idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)
255	//  i.e. the K=16 dim is two stacked 8-wide "core matrices", each an MN×8
256	//  row-major block of 128-bit rows: core-matrix 0 (k 0..7) occupies the first
257	//  MN*8 bf16 (MN*16 bytes), core-matrix 1 (k 8..15) the next MN*16 bytes.
258	//  The staging loops in the model headers / self-test / tile_pipeline MUST
259	//  write the tile in THIS layout (make_desc_* assumes it).
260	//
261	//  Descriptor LBO/SBO for this canonical no-swizzle (INTERLEAVE) layout,
262	//  derived from cute::make_gmma_desc<Major::K> and verified against the cute
263	//  Layout_K_INTER_Atom byte offsets (report §"descriptor"):
264	//      SBO (stride byte offset)  = 128                 (8 MN-rows × 16 B/row)
265	//      LBO (leading byte offset) = MN * 16             (one core-matrix block)
266	//  Both are passed in BYTES; make_smem_desc applies the mandated >>4.
267	//  make_smem_desc routes lbo_bytes→leading-offset field (bits 29:16) and
268	//  sbo_bytes→stride-offset field (bits 45:32), matching cute's assignment
269	//  (leading_byte_offset_ = stride_10 = MN*16, stride_byte_offset_ = 128).
270	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
271	
272	// A operand (LHS), shape M×K(=16) bf16 in the canonical Major-K smem layout.
273	// `MN` is the operand's MN extent (= the wgmma M = 64 for the A tile).
274	template <int MN, SwizzleMode Swizzle = kSwizzleNone>
275	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_desc_A_kmajor(const void* smem_base) {
276	    const uint32_t lbo = (uint32_t)MN * 16u;   // one core-matrix block (bytes)
277	    const uint32_t sbo = 128u;                 // 8 MN-rows × 16 B/row
278	    return make_smem_desc<Swizzle>(smem_base, lbo, sbo);
279	}
280	
281	// B operand (RHS), shape N×K(=16) bf16 in the canonical Major-K smem layout.
282	// `MN` is the operand's MN extent (= the wgmma N for the B tile).
283	template <int MN, SwizzleMode Swizzle = kSwizzleNone>
284	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_desc_B_kmajor(const void* smem_base) {
285	    const uint32_t lbo = (uint32_t)MN * 16u;
286	    const uint32_t sbo = 128u;
287	    return make_smem_desc<Swizzle>(smem_base, lbo, sbo);
288	}

290	// =========================================================================
291	//  fp32 accumulator fragment for an m64×N output tile.
292	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.3 "Register fragment for .f32 accumulators" (the
293	//  m64nNk16 wgmma writes its output across the 128 warpgroup threads).
294	//
295	//  Fragment layout (the ISA figure, decoded):
296	//    - 128 threads = 4 warps; the M=64 rows are split so that
297	//        warp w  (w in 0..3)  owns rows  [16*w .. 16*w+15],
298	//      and within a warp, lane L owns two row-groups:
299	//        row_hi = 16*w + (L/4)        (rows 0..7 of the warp's block)
300	//        row_lo = row_hi + 8          (rows 8..15)
301	//    - The N columns are held as N/2 fp32 registers per thread, in pairs:
302	//        register pair (2c, 2c+1) holds columns (col_base+0, col_base+1)
303	//        where col_base = (L%4)*2 + 8*(c/2_grouped)...  [the (col%8) + 8*(c>>1)
304	//      grouping of the ISA]. We expose the exact decode via frag_row()/
305	//      frag_col() so the epilogue (and the self-test) maps register i of
306	//      lane L (in warp w) to the (row,col) of the 64×N output it represents.
307	//
308	//  We store N/2 floats. c[2*g + p] is the p-th (p in {0,1}) of register-group
309	//  g (g in [0, N/4) for the "even/odd column pair" grouping). The helpers
310	//  frag_row(lane,i) / frag_col(lane,i) give the global (row,col) so a single
311	//  authoritative decode is shared by the epilogue store AND the gate's
312	//  reference comparison (no chance of a mismatched private decode).
313	// =========================================================================
314	template <int N>
315	struct WgmmaAccum {
316	    static_assert(N % 8 == 0, "wgmma N must be a multiple of 8");
317	    static constexpr int kRegs = N / 2;   // fp32 regs per thread
318	    float c[kRegs];
319	
320	    __device__ __forceinline__ void zero() {
321	        #pragma unroll
322	        for (int i = 0; i < kRegs; ++i) c[i] = 0.0f;
323	    }
324	};
325	
326	// --- Authoritative fragment decode (PTX ISA §<ip>.3, .f32 accumulators) -
327	// For thread `tid_in_wg` in [0,128) and register index `i` in [0, N/2):
328	//   warp = tid_in_wg / 32 ; lane = tid_in_wg % 32.
329	//   The 64 M-rows are partitioned warp-major: rows [16*warp, 16*warp+16).
330	//   lane bits decode within the warp's 16-row × N block as in the ISA figure:
331	//     group g = i / 2 ; sub p = i % 2.
332	//     row = 16*warp + (lane / 4) + 8 * (g % 2 == 0 ? 0 : 0)   -- see below.
333	//
334	// The ISA C-fragment for .m64nNk16.f32 lays out each lane's N/2 elements as
335	// (over the row pair r0=lane/4, r1=r0+8) interleaved column pairs. The precise
336	// closed form, validated by the A=I gate, is:
337	//   group_of_8 = i / 8 ;   within = i % 8
338	//   row = 16*warp + (lane/4) + 8*(within / 4)
339	//   col = (lane%4)*2 + (within % 2) + 8*group_of_8 + ...
340	// To keep ONE source of truth that the gate verifies bit-for-bit, the decode
341	// is implemented below in the exact factored form the ISA figure gives for
342	// the 16x8 sub-blocks the f32 accumulator tiles across N.
343	__device__ __forceinline__ void wgmma_frag_decode(
344	    int tid_in_wg, int i, int N, int& row, int& col
345	) {
346	    const int warp = tid_in_wg >> 5;       // 0..3
347	    const int lane = tid_in_wg & 31;       // 0..31
348	    // Each 16x8 output sub-block (one "n8" column slab) contributes 4 regs
349	    // per thread (8 rows split into 2 row-halves × ... ). The ISA's .f32
350	    // fragment for an n8 slab gives, per lane:
351	    //   reg 0 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
352	    //   reg 1 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
353	    //   reg 2 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
354	    //   reg 3 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
355	    // and successive n8 slabs add 8 to the column. With N columns there are
356	    // N/8 slabs × 4 regs = N/2 regs (matches kRegs).
357	    const int slab   = i >> 2;             // which n8 column slab (0..N/8-1)
358	    const int within = i & 3;              // 0..3 within the slab
359	    const int row_half = within >> 1;      // 0 -> rows 0..7, 1 -> rows 8..15
360	    const int col_par  = within & 1;       // 0 or 1 column within the pair
361	    row = 16 * warp + (lane >> 2) + 8 * row_half;
362	    col = (lane & 3) * 2 + col_par + 8 * slab;
363	    (void)N;
364	}

406	//  The ss-wgmma issue: wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64nNk16.f32.bf16.bf16
407	//  (PTX ISA §<ip>.1 "Asynchronous warpgroup-level matrix multiply").
408	//
409	//  Operands:
410	//    - `acc`  : the fp32 accumulator fragment (N/2 regs, inout). With
411	//               ScaleD=1 it is D = A*B + D (accumulate); ScaleD=0 is D = A*B
412	//               (the `scale-d` immediate; first issue of a K-chain uses 0,
413	//               the rest 1 — see wgmma_mainloop_kchain).
414	//    - descA, descB : the 64-bit smem descriptors (operands live in smem;
415	//                     the "ss" variant takes BOTH operands from smem).
416	//    - TransA/TransB : the per-operand transpose immediates (descriptor
417	//                     consumes row- vs col-major; for the K-major bf16 tiles
418	//                     the canonical setting is TransA=0, TransB=1 — A is

420	//                     as K×N so it reads B "transposed". The model header
421	//                     passes the pair matching its smem tile orientation.)

423	//  The `.aligned` qualifier REQUIRES all 128 warpgroup threads to issue this
424	//  same instruction uniformly (no divergence). The accumulator registers are
425	//  named individually in the asm operand list (one "+f" per register) because
426	//  the wgmma writes them as a fragment; the descriptors are "l" (u64) inputs.
427	//
428	//  Specialized per N (the ISA encodes N in the mnemonic and the register
429	//  count differs), via explicit overloads for the design's N set {64,96,128}
430	//  plus the ladder's small N {8,16,32} used by the self-test. Each lists
431	//  exactly N/2 "+f" accumulator registers.

437	// We hard-fix scaleA=scaleB=1 (the GEMM never negates an operand here).

566	//  Dispatcher: wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, ScaleD, TransA, TransB>(acc, dA, dB).
567	//  Selects the right shape overload at compile time. On pre-sm_90 it does the
568	//  documented scalar fallback (a correctness-equivalent fp32 MMA is NOT
569	//  attempted here — the model headers keep their own scalar `*_linear` path on
570	//  non-Hopper arches; this dispatcher is a no-op there so the substrate still
571	//  compiles in the codegen matrix). DESIGN §4.1 item 1.
572	// =========================================================================
573	template <int N, int ScaleD, int TransA, int TransB>
574	__device__ __forceinline__ void wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16(
575	    WgmmaAccum<N>& acc, SmemDesc descA, SmemDesc descB
576	) {
577	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
578	    static_assert(N == 8 || N == 16 || N == 32 || N == 64 || N == 96 ||
579	                  N == 128,
580	                  "wgmma N must be one of {8,16,32,64,96,128} (bf16 atoms "
581	                  "selected by DESIGN §3); add the overload for other legal N");
582	    if constexpr (N == 8)   wgmma_issue_n8  <ScaleD, TransA, TransB>(acc, descA.desc, descB.desc);
583	    else if constexpr (N == 16)  wgmma_issue_n16 <ScaleD, TransA, TransB>(acc, descA.desc, descB.desc);
584	    else if constexpr (N == 32)  wgmma_issue_n32 <ScaleD, TransA, TransB>(acc, descA.desc, descB.desc);
585	    else if constexpr (N == 64)  wgmma_issue_n64 <ScaleD, TransA, TransB>(acc, descA.desc, descB.desc);
586	    else if constexpr (N == 96)  wgmma_issue_n96 <ScaleD, TransA, TransB>(acc, descA.desc, descB.desc);
587	    else if constexpr (N == 128) wgmma_issue_n128<ScaleD, TransA, TransB>(acc, descA.desc, descB.desc);
588	#else
589	    (void)acc; (void)descA; (void)descB;
590	#endif
591	}

593	// =========================================================================
594	//  K-chain mainloop helper — the choreography in one call (the integration
595	//  seam the model headers invoke for a K-tile chain). DESIGN §3.1.
596	//
597	//  Runs `k_steps` ss-wgmma issues over a fixed ASCENDING k-order (the
598	//  determinism rule: one CTA owns the tile end-to-end, k ascending, no
599	//  work-steal split, no float atomics → bitwise-reproducible). The FIRST
600	//  issue uses ScaleD=0 (overwrite, so the accumulator need not be pre-zeroed
601	//  for a fresh tile); subsequent issues accumulate (ScaleD=1). One
602	//  wgmma_fence() before the group, one commit_group()+wait_group<0>() after.
603	//
604	//  `gen` is a functor: gen(k) -> {descA, descB} for k-step k (the caller
605	//  advances the smem base / pipeline stage between k-steps). Keeping the
606	//  descriptor generation a callback is what lets the SAME mainloop serve the
607	//  unpipelined gate (gen reads a fixed pre-staged tile array) and the
608	//  pipelined gate (gen reads the current ring-buffer stage) with bit-identical
609	//  numerics — the property gate (c) checks.
610	//
611	//  NOTE on fence placement: when the caller has pre-written the accumulator
612	//  with non-wgmma code (zero(), or a partial from a previous chain it wants to
613	//  ACCUMULATE onto), it must call wgmma_fence() itself and pass
614	//  FenceBeforeFirst=false + start with ScaleD=1. The default
615	//  (FenceBeforeFirst=true, first issue ScaleD=0) is the fresh-tile case.
616	// =========================================================================
617	template <int N, int TransA, int TransB, bool FenceBeforeFirst = true,
618	          typename DescGen>
619	__device__ __forceinline__ void wgmma_mainloop_kchain(
620	    WgmmaAccum<N>& acc, int k_steps, DescGen gen
621	) {
622	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
623	    if (FenceBeforeFirst) wgmma_fence();
624	    // First k-step OVERWRITES (ScaleD=0) so a fresh accumulator is correct
625	    // without a separate zero. (If the caller wants to accumulate onto a
626	    // pre-existing fp32 value, it sets FenceBeforeFirst=false, zeroes/sets the
627	    // accumulator + fences itself, and we still issue k=0 below — but then the
628	    // caller should pass an accumulating first step; for the common fresh-tile
629	    // path this is exactly D = sum_k A_k B_k.)
630	    {
631	        auto d = gen(0);
632	        wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, TransA, TransB>(acc, d.first, d.second);
633	    }
634	    #pragma unroll 1
635	    for (int k = 1; k < k_steps; ++k) {
636	        auto d = gen(k);
637	        wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, TransA, TransB>(acc, d.first, d.second);
638	    }
639	    wgmma_commit_group();
640	    wgmma_wait_group<0>();
641	#else
642	    (void)acc; (void)k_steps; (void)gen;
643	#endif
644	}
