99	// =========================================================================
100	//  Ring-buffer geometry for one (A 64×16 + B N×16) bf16 stage.
101	//  A tile: 64×16 bf16 = 2048 B.  B tile: N×16 bf16 = N*32 B.
102	//  All tiles K-contiguous (row-major), matching make_desc_{A,B}_kmajor.
103	// =========================================================================
104	template <int N>
105	struct TileGeom {
106	    static constexpr int kAElems   = 64 * kWgmmaAtomK;        // 1024
107	    static constexpr int kBElems   = N  * kWgmmaAtomK;        // N*16
108	    static constexpr int kABytes   = kAElems * (int)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16);
109	    static constexpr int kBBytes   = kBElems * (int)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16);
110	    static constexpr int kStageBytes = kABytes + kBBytes;
111	    static constexpr uint32_t kARowStride = kWgmmaAtomK * (uint32_t)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16); // 32
112	    static constexpr uint32_t kBRowStride = kWgmmaAtomK * (uint32_t)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16); // 32
113	    // tx-bytes for the stage's two cp.async transactions (full barrier expects).
114	    static constexpr int kStageTxBytes = kStageBytes;
115	};
116	
117	// =========================================================================
118	//  TilePipeline — the Depth-stage ring + its mbarriers.
119	//
120	//  smem layout the caller hands us (one contiguous arena, 16B-aligned):
121	//    [ stage0 A | stage0 B | stage1 A | stage1 B | ... | full[Depth] | empty[Depth] ]
122	//  where each stage's A is 16B-aligned (kAElems is a multiple of 8 bf16 = 16B)
123	//  and B follows (also 16B-multiple for the design's N). The two mbarrier
124	//  arrays are 8-byte words.
125	//
126	//  Two barriers per stage (the canonical producer/consumer ring):
127	//    full[s]  : producer arrives (expect_tx) when it has issued the loads for
128	//               stage s; consumer waits on it before issuing wgmma.
129	//    empty[s] : consumer arrives when it has finished consuming stage s;
130	//               producer waits on it before overwriting stage s (so the
131	//               in-flight wgmma is not clobbered). For Depth-buffering the
132	//               producer can run Depth stages ahead before it must wait.
133	//
134	//  Phase parity: each barrier flips parity every time its expected arrivals
135	//  complete. We track per-stage parity bits for full and empty.
136	// =========================================================================
137	//  NOTE on storage: Mbarrier (warp_specialize.cuh) is a thin wrapper around a
138	//  single smem word and has only an `explicit Mbarrier(ull*)` constructor (no
139	//  default ctor). To avoid needing a default-constructible barrier array, we
140	//  store ONLY the barrier-word base pointer and construct an Mbarrier
141	//  on-demand via full(s) / empty(s) — a zero-cost wrapper around the word.
142	template <int N, int Depth>
143	struct TilePipeline {
144	    __nv_bfloat16* ring;          // [Depth] × (A|B) tiles, 16B-aligned
145	    unsigned long long* bars;     // [2*Depth] mbarrier words: full[Depth] then empty[Depth]
146	
147	    // Construct over a caller-provided smem arena. `arena` points at the start
148	    // of the ring (must be 16B-aligned). The barrier words follow the tiles.
149	    __device__ __forceinline__ TilePipeline(void* arena)
150	        : ring(reinterpret_cast<__nv_bfloat16*>(arena)),
151	          bars(reinterpret_cast<unsigned long long*>(
152	              reinterpret_cast<char*>(arena) +
153	              (size_t)Depth * TileGeom<N>::kStageBytes)) {}
154	
155	    __device__ __forceinline__ Mbarrier full(int s)  { return Mbarrier(bars + s); }
156	    __device__ __forceinline__ Mbarrier empty(int s) { return Mbarrier(bars + Depth + s); }
157	
158	    __device__ __forceinline__ __nv_bfloat16* stageA(int s) {
159	        return ring + (size_t)s * (TileGeom<N>::kAElems + TileGeom<N>::kBElems);
160	    }
161	    __device__ __forceinline__ __nv_bfloat16* stageB(int s) {
162	        return stageA(s) + TileGeom<N>::kAElems;
163	    }
164	
165	    // Bytes the caller must allocate as dynamic smem for this pipeline.
166	    static constexpr size_t smem_bytes() {
167	        return (size_t)Depth * TileGeom<N>::kStageBytes +
168	               (size_t)2 * Depth * sizeof(unsigned long long);
169	    }
170	
171	    // Init the barriers (one thread of the block). Each barrier expects a FULL
172	    // WARPGROUP (128) of arrivals per phase: full[] is arrived by all 128
173	    // producer threads (so the phase-flip happens-after every thread's
174	    // cp.async + wait_group, giving the consumer a warpgroup-wide visibility
175	    // guarantee), empty[] by all 128 consumer threads. (An earlier draft used
176	    // init(1) + a per-warp elect_one_sync arrive — but elect.sync elects one
177	    // leader PER WARP, so 4 warps produced 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier,
178	    // flipping the phase an even number of times and DEADLOCKING the consumer's
179	    // try_wait.parity. count=128 + all-threads-arrive is the correct contract.)
180	    __device__ __forceinline__ void init_barriers() {
181	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
182	            #pragma unroll
183	            for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) {
184	                full(s).init(128);
185	                empty(s).init(128);
186	            }
187	        }
188	    }
189	};
190	
191	// =========================================================================
192	//  Producer-side staging of ONE K-tile (stage `slot`, k-index `k`) via
193	//  cp.async (DESIGN §4.2 WG0). Issues 16-byte cp.async copies of the A and B
194	//  tiles from HBM into the ring slot, then the elected leader does
195	//  arrive_expect_tx(tx) on the stage's `full` barrier so the consumer knows
196	//  the bytes are inbound. cp.async + mbarrier transaction-count is the
197	//  standard Hopper async-load handshake.
198	//
199	//  NOTE: this uses cp.async (.cg.16), NOT TMA — DESIGN §4.1 item 3 makes TMA
200	//  explicitly phase-2; phase-1 staging is cp.async (already overlaps load
201	//  latency). For cp.async the transaction completion is signalled via
202	//  cp.async.mbarrier.arrive (the bytes are counted by the barrier). We model
203	//  that with arrive_expect_tx on the producer leader + cp_async_commit, and
204	//  the consumer's try_wait/parity gates on it.
205	// =========================================================================
206	template <int N, int Depth>
207	__device__ __forceinline__ void pipeline_produce_ktile(
208	    TilePipeline<N, Depth>& pipe, int slot, int k,
209	    const __nv_bfloat16* gA, const __nv_bfloat16* gB, int /*k_steps*/
210	) {
211	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
212	    const int wtid = threadIdx.x & 127;          // 0..127 within WG0
213	    __nv_bfloat16* dA = pipe.stageA(slot);
214	    __nv_bfloat16* dB = pipe.stageB(slot);
215	    const __nv_bfloat16* sA = gA + (size_t)k * TileGeom<N>::kAElems;  // row-major MxK
216	    const __nv_bfloat16* sB = gB + (size_t)k * TileGeom<N>::kBElems;  // row-major NxK
217	
218	    // 16B (8 bf16) cp.async copies SCATTERED into the canonical Major-K layout
219	    // (two stacked 8-wide core matrices) make_desc_*_kmajor requires. A global
220	    // row (mn, 0..15) splits into two 16B halves: half 0 (k 0..7) lands at
221	    // mn*8, half 1 (k 8..15) at MN*8 + mn*8 — both 16B-aligned. kVec=8 bf16.
222	    constexpr int kVec = 16 / (int)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16);   // 8 bf16 / 16B
223	    // A: MN=64. 64 rows × 2 halves = 128 vectors.
224	    constexpr int kAHalves = 64 * (kWgmmaAtomK / kVec);     // 64*2 = 128
225	    for (int v = wtid; v < kAHalves; v += 128) {
226	        const int mn = v >> 1;                  // 0..63
227	        const int half = v & 1;                 // 0 or 1
228	        const __nv_bfloat16* src = sA + (size_t)mn * kWgmmaAtomK + (size_t)half * kVec;
229	        __nv_bfloat16* dst = dA + (size_t)half * (64 * kVec) + (size_t)mn * kVec;
230	        prim::cp_async_cg_16(dst, src);
231	    }
232	    // B: MN=N. N rows × 2 halves vectors.
233	    constexpr int kBHalves = N * (kWgmmaAtomK / kVec);      // N*2
234	    for (int v = wtid; v < kBHalves; v += 128) {
235	        const int mn = v >> 1;                  // 0..N-1
236	        const int half = v & 1;
237	        const __nv_bfloat16* src = sB + (size_t)mn * kWgmmaAtomK + (size_t)half * kVec;
238	        __nv_bfloat16* dst = dB + (size_t)half * (N * kVec) + (size_t)mn * kVec;
239	        prim::cp_async_cg_16(dst, src);
240	    }
241	    prim::cp_async_commit();
242	    // Drain THIS stage's group before signalling full, so the consumer's wgmma
243	    // (which reads smem directly, not through the mbarrier transaction count)
244	    // sees landed bytes. cp.async.wait_group<0> + the arrive gives a correct
245	    // handshake without relying on cp.async.mbarrier.arrive byte-counting
246	    // (which would require the .mbarrier.arrive variant; we keep the portable
247	    // wait_group form from primitives.cuh and use the mbarrier purely as the
248	    // cross-warpgroup ready signal). DESIGN §4.2: one async-proxy fence per
249	    // hand-off.
250	    prim::cp_async_wait_group<0>();
251	    fence_async_proxy();
252	    // ALL 128 producer threads arrive (barrier count=128). Each thread's
253	    // arrive happens-after its own cp.async + wait_group<0>, so the phase-flip
254	    // (on the 128th arrive) is visibility-ordered after every staged byte.
255	    pipe.full(slot).arrive();       // signal: stage `slot` is ready to consume
256	#else
257	    (void)pipe; (void)slot; (void)k; (void)gA; (void)gB;
258	#endif
259	}

261	// =========================================================================
262	//  tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16 — the turnkey single-CTA pipelined GEMM.
263	//  blockDim.x = 256: WG0 = producer (tid 0..127), WG1 = consumer (128..255).
264	//  DESIGN §4.2 producer/consumer structure, §4.3 occupancy budget.
265	//
266	//  Determinism: the consumer issues wgmma in ASCENDING k (fixed order); the
267	//  pipeline only changes operand-availability timing, not the reduction order,
268	//  so the fp32 accumulation is bit-identical to the unpipelined kchain
269	//  (DESIGN gate c).
270	// =========================================================================
271	template <int N, int Depth>
272	__device__ __forceinline__ void tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16(
273	    const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ gA,
274	    const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ gB,
275	    float* __restrict__ gD, int k_steps
276	) {
277	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
278	    extern __shared__ char smem_raw[];
279	    // 16B-align the ring arena.
280	    uintptr_t base = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(smem_raw);
281	    uintptr_t aligned = (base + 15u) & ~uintptr_t(15u);
282	    TilePipeline<N, Depth> pipe(reinterpret_cast<void*>(aligned));
283	    pipe.init_barriers();
284	    __syncthreads();
285	
286	    const int warpgroup = threadIdx.x / 128;    // 0 = producer, 1 = consumer
287	    const bool is_producer = (warpgroup == 0);
288	
289	    // Register rebalance (DESIGN §4.2): producer few regs, consumer many.
290	    // Guarded by SG_TUNED_*_REGS != 0 (0 disables for portability/debug).
291	#if (SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS != 0) && (SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS != 0)
292	    if (is_producer) warpgroup_reg_dealloc<SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS>();
293	    else             warpgroup_reg_alloc  <SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS>();
294	#endif
295	
296	    if (is_producer) {
297	        // Producer: stage every K-tile in ascending k. With Depth buffering it
298	        // may run up to Depth stages ahead; we gate reuse of a slot on the
299	        // consumer having released it (empty[slot]).
300	        unsigned empty_parity[Depth];
301	        #pragma unroll
302	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) empty_parity[s] = 0u;
303	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
304	            const int slot = k % Depth;
305	            // For k >= Depth, the slot was used by k-Depth; wait until the
306	            // consumer released it (empty barrier) before overwriting.
307	            if (k >= Depth) {
308	                pipe.empty(slot).wait(empty_parity[slot]);
309	                empty_parity[slot] ^= 1u;
310	            }
311	            pipeline_produce_ktile<N, Depth>(pipe, slot, k, gA, gB, k_steps);
312	        }
313	    } else {
314	        // Consumer: wgmma over each staged K-tile in ascending k. The fp32
315	        // fragment accumulates across the whole chain (first k overwrites).
316	        WgmmaAccum<N> acc;
317	        unsigned full_parity[Depth];
318	        #pragma unroll
319	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) full_parity[s] = 0u;
320	
321	        // We can't use the kchain helper directly (it expects all descriptors
322	        // available); instead we inline the SAME choreography: one fence, then
323	        // k=0 overwrite / k>0 accumulate, commit+wait at the end. Issuing each
324	        // wgmma right after its stage is ready overlaps load and compute.
325	        wgmma_fence();
326	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
327	            const int slot = k % Depth;
328	            pipe.full(slot).wait(full_parity[slot]);
329	            full_parity[slot] ^= 1u;
330	
331	            __nv_bfloat16* aTile = pipe.stageA(slot);
332	            __nv_bfloat16* bTile = pipe.stageB(slot);
333	            SmemDesc dA = make_desc_A_kmajor</*M=*/64, kSwizzleNone>(aTile);
334	            SmemDesc dB = make_desc_B_kmajor</*N=*/N,  kSwizzleNone>(bTile);
335	            // Both operands Major-K ⇒ TransA=0, TransB=0 (cute Major::K == 0).
336	            if (k == 0) {
337	                wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, /*TransA=*/0, /*TransB=*/0>(acc, dA, dB);
338	            } else {
339	                wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, /*TransA=*/0, /*TransB=*/0>(acc, dA, dB);
340	            }
341	            // Commit + wait THIS issue before releasing the slot, so the
342	            // producer does not overwrite operands the async wgmma still reads.
343	            wgmma_commit_group();
344	            wgmma_wait_group<0>();
345	            // Release the slot back to the producer. ALL 128 consumer threads
346	            // arrive (barrier count=128) — see init_barriers: the per-warp elect
347	            // would give 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier and deadlock.
348	            pipe.empty(slot).arrive();
349	        }
350	
351	        // Epilogue: store the fp32 fragment. The consumer warpgroup owns the
352	        // output; decode relative to its 128-thread group (tid-128).
353	        const int tid_in_wg = threadIdx.x - 128;
354	        #pragma unroll
355	        for (int i = 0; i < WgmmaAccum<N>::kRegs; ++i) {
356	            int row, col;
357	            wgmma_frag_decode(tid_in_wg, i, N, row, col);
358	            gD[row * N + col] = acc.c[i];
359	        }
360	    }
361	#else
362	    (void)gA; (void)gB; (void)gD; (void)k_steps;
363	#endif
364	}
365	
366	}}} // namespace sg::sm90::wgs

1	// csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_adamw.cu — PHASE 1 host-launcher TU for the
2	// TRUE L3 fused (transformer_decoder × adamw) megakernel.
3	//
4	// WHY A SEPARATE .cu (the 33-cell pattern): dispatch.cpp is HOST-compiled (it is
5	// a .cpp in the cpp_extension source list), so it cannot host <<<>>> launches,
6	// __global__ kernels, or device intrinsics. This nvcc-compiled TU (setup.py
7	// globs csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cu) owns ALL of that. It exposes ONE non-template host
8	// launcher whose boundary signature is decomposed to plain pointers/ints + the
9	// FusedScalars POD — NO header-only types (DecoderTokenCtx/FusedOptState) cross
10	// the boundary — so dispatch.cpp can `extern`-declare it using only the mirror
11	// structs it already has (sg::fused::PersistentContext, sg::fused::sm90::
12	// FusedScalars). The FQN + layout match → the mangling matches → it links.
13	//
14	// Inside (where the device header IS visible) it builds FusedOptState +
15	// DecoderTokenCtx and calls launch_fused_decoder_megakernel<OptId::AdamW>, which
16	// runs the REAL decoder fwd+bwd + AdamW as one persistent kernel (no surrogate,
17	// no intermediate launches). See fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh +
18	// model_stages_decoder.cuh (transcribed from the verified oracle).
19	
20	#include "csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh"
21	
22	namespace sg { namespace fused { namespace sm90 {
23	
24	cudaError_t mega_decoder_real_adamw(
25	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
26	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
27	        float* state, float* grad, float* workspace, float* loss_out,
28	        const int* sizes, const int* offsets,
29	        float lr, int step, const FusedScalars& scalars, cudaStream_t stream) {
30	    // sizes/offsets are unused on this path (the kernel reads the generated
31	    // __constant__ kDecSizes/kDecOffsets directly); kept in the signature for ABI
32	    // symmetry with the surrogate cells and forward-compat. Silence the warning.
33	    (void)sizes; (void)offsets;
34	
35	    const int64_t total = kDecTotalElems;
36	    // AdamW state binding: state = [m | v | extra] (3*total) + 1 trailing loss
37	    // slot. extra is unused by AdamW (rebase_state<AdamW> guards it out).
38	    FusedOptState st;
39	    st.exp_avg    = state;
40	    st.exp_avg_sq = state + total;
41	    apply_scalars(st, scalars);   // FULL scalar set (un-frozen bc1/bc2/...)
42	    st.lr = lr;
43	
44	    DecoderTokenCtx tok;
45	    tok.tokens    = tokens;
46	    tok.targets   = targets;
47	    tok.B         = B;
48	    tok.workspace = workspace;
49	    tok.loss_out  = loss_out;
50	
51	    return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel<OptId::AdamW>(
52	        ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream);
53	}
54	
55	}}}  // namespace sg::fused::sm90

1	# Fused-megakernel component contract (portability spec)
2	
3	Owner requirement (2026-06-09): every (model × optimizer × arch) configuration —
4	all 3 models × 11 optimizers — composes into ONE persistent megakernel binary,
5	and the building blocks are **individually portable**: a third project lifts the
6	headers and instantiates a fused trainer without dragging this repo along. The
7	meta-programming lives in headers; the dispatch layer is generated and is the
8	only composition seam.
9	
10	## Component taxonomy (header-only, self-contained)
11	
12	| component | header(s) | contract |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| **Substrate** | `csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh` | `PersistentContext` (task counter, grid barrier, generation), one-CTA-per-SM persistent launch idiom. Depends on CUDA runtime only. |
15	| **Optimizer math** | `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` (×11) | Pure per-element apply math (`<opt>_step(...)`), no CUDA dependencies beyond `__device__` qualifiers, no state allocation, no I/O. Single source of truth — everything else `#include`s these (enforced by `scripts/check_math_single_source.py`). Already portable as-is. |
16	| **Optimizer tails** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh` | `apply_optimizer<OptId>(FusedOptState&, FusedScalars const&, ...)` — templates composing the algorithm headers into megakernel stages. Consumes the documented POD structs only. |
17	| **Model stages** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_<model>.cuh` (decoder / vit / mamba3 — ONE HEADER PER MODEL, not a monolith) | Provides `model_<m>_forward_stage<Dims>` and `model_<m>_backward_stage<Dims>`: batch-slice-local fwd/bwd with all activations CTA-local, writing per-CTA weight-grad partials to a caller-provided workspace. Templated on compile-time dims (d_model, n_layers, n_heads, seq, vocab). Includes ONLY the substrate header + CUDA. No globals, no repo build flags (every `SG_TUNED_*` consumed via `#ifndef` defaults). |
18	| **Composition** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_megakernel.cuh` | `launch_fused_megakernel<ModelId, OptId, Tier>` — stage pipeline: fwd → bwd → grid barrier → deterministic weight-grad reduction → optimizer tail. The only place stages and tails meet. |
19	| **Cells** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_<model>_<opt>.cu` (×33) | GENERATED 36-line instantiations (`megakernel_codegen.py`). Never hand-edited. |
20	| **Dispatch** | `csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp` + generated `fused_wired_cells.inc` / `fused_dispatch_table.inc` | `(model, optimizer, arch) → cell` routing. Generated from the same enumeration as the cells, so it cannot drift. Loud-gated: unwired/unready cells throw, never silently degrade. |
21	
22	## Portability rules (apply to every new/edited component)
23	1. **Self-containment**: a component header compiles with `#include <cuda_runtime.h>`
24	   + its declared includes only. Include-what-you-use; no transitive reliance.
25	2. **No hidden state**: no globals, no statics with side effects; all state flows
26	   through the documented POD structs (`PersistentContext`, `FusedOptState`,
27	   `FusedScalars`) or explicit pointers.
28	3. **Compile-time configuration only via documented template params or
29	   `#ifndef`-defaulted macros** (`SG_TUNED_*`); absent definitions must yield a
30	   correct (if untuned) kernel.
31	4. **The lift test**: copying `megakernel_common.cuh` + one `model_stage_*.cuh`
32	   + `opt_components.cuh` + the relevant `csrc/algorithms/*.h` into a fresh
33	   project and instantiating `launch_fused_megakernel<M,O,Tier>` must build and
34	   run. Each phase's validation includes compiling a minimal out-of-tree TU
35	   (tests/hw/test_component_portability.cu) that includes ONLY those headers.
36	5. **Generated artifacts are never edited by hand** — change the generator,
37	   regenerate everything, `git diff` must be generator-consistent.
38	6. **No placeholder math** on any wired path (owner no-suppression directive);
39	   surrogate stages exist only behind explicit unreadiness gates and throw at
40	   dispatch.
41	
42	## Phase status
43	- Phase 1 (in flight): real decoder fwd+bwd stages, validated vs eager — lands
44	  in `model_stages.cuh`, then is split per-model per this contract.
45	- Phase 2: vit + mamba3 stage headers (built against this contract natively).
46	- Phase 3: optimizer precompute stages in-kernel for the 9 non-trivial tails;
47	  SuperGrok2's CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta as in-kernel stages (the full
48	  "vit×sg2 in one binary").

107	# ── reference + tolerance ────────────────────────────────────────────────
108	#
109	# The wgmma computes  D[m,n] = sum_k A[m,k] * B[n,k]  with bf16 inputs and an
110	# fp32 accumulator (B is stored N×K row-major and read transposed → D = A @ B^T
111	# over the stored tiles). The faithful reference is the SAME contraction done in
112	# fp32 on the bf16-ROUNDED inputs: cast A,B to bf16 (both sides), then upcast to
113	# fp32 and matmul. bf16 inputs are then exact on both sides and bf16×bf16
114	# products are exact in fp32; the ONLY residual is fp32 ACCUMULATION ORDER
115	# (hardware k-order vs torch). The reference is computed on CPU in fp64 (and in
116	# fp32 on-GPU with TF32 DISABLED) so the reference itself carries no tensor-core
117	# imprecision.
118	#
119	# Tolerance derivation (stated, not guessed): with K total accumulation steps,
120	# the fp32 accumulation round-off is bounded ≈ K · ε_fp32 · max|partial|, with
121	# ε_fp32 = 2^-24 ≈ 6e-8. For K ≤ 512 and unit-scale operands the absolute error
122	# bound is ≈ 512 · 6e-8 · O(K) ≈ a few e-3 worst case; in practice (random
123	# ±1 operands, well-conditioned) max-abs-err is ≤ ~1e-3. We therefore gate at
124	# atol=2e-3, rtol=2e-3. A max-err at the ~1e-2 level would indicate a BUG
125	# (fragment-layout / transpose / leaked TF32), not bf16 noise — we do NOT loosen
126	# the tolerance to absorb that.
127	_ATOL = 2e-3
128	_RTOL = 2e-3
129	
130	
131	def _disable_tf32():
132	    # The on-GPU fp32 reference must NOT run on TF32 tensor cores or it loses
133	    # ~10 mantissa bits and the tolerance becomes meaningless.
134	    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
135	    torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False
136	
137	
138	def _make_AB(N, k_steps, seed):
139	    """A: [k_steps,64,16] bf16, B: [k_steps,N,16] bf16. Returns (A,B, A_flat,B_flat)."""
140	    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
141	    A = (torch.randn(k_steps, 64, 16, generator=g, device="cuda",
142	                     dtype=torch.float32)).to(torch.bfloat16)
143	    B = (torch.randn(k_steps, N, 16, generator=g, device="cuda",
144	                     dtype=torch.float32)).to(torch.bfloat16)
145	    return A, B
146	
147	
148	def _reference(A, B):
149	    """fp64 CPU reference: D[m,n] = sum_{k_step,k} A[k_step,m,k]·B[k_step,n,k]."""
150	    Ad = A.double().cpu()   # [ks,64,16]
151	    Bd = B.double().cpu()   # [ks,N,16]
152	    # contract over (k_step, 16): einsum gives D[m,n] = Σ_{s,k} A[s,m,k] B[s,n,k]
153	    D = torch.einsum("smk,snk->mn", Ad, Bd)
154	    return D   # [64, N] fp64 on CPU
155	
156	
157	def _run_tile(mod, A, B, N, k_steps):
158	    A_flat = A.reshape(-1).contiguous()
159	    B_flat = B.reshape(-1).contiguous()
160	    return mod.gemm_tile(A_flat, B_flat, N, k_steps)   # [64,N] fp32 cuda
161	
162	
163	def _max_err(D_dev, D_ref):
164	    d = D_dev.double().cpu()
165	    return (d - D_ref).abs().max().item()

168	# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
169	#  LOCALIZATION: A = I (identity), single K-tile. Output must equal B exactly
170	#  (the 64×16 identity-prefix times B). This isolates fragment-layout /
171	#  descriptor / transpose bugs: any permuted output element points straight at
172	#  the mapping. Run first; if this fails, the random-input gates are noise.
173	# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
174	@_GATE
175	def test_a_identity_localization():
176	    mod = _build_module()
177	    _disable_tf32()
178	    N = 16
179	    k_steps = 1
180	    # A is 64×16. Make it select row r of B^T... we want D = A @ B^T with B
181	    # stored N×16. Set A[m,k] = 1 if (m==k) else 0 over the 16-col K, so for
182	    # m<16: D[m,n] = sum_k A[m,k]·B[n,k] = B[n,m]. i.e. D = B^T (first 16 rows).
183	    A = torch.zeros(1, 64, 16, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
184	    for i in range(16):
185	        A[0, i, i] = 1.0
186	    A = A.to(torch.bfloat16)
187	    B = torch.arange(N * 16, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32).reshape(1, N, 16)
188	    B = (B / 97.0).to(torch.bfloat16)   # distinct, bf16-representable-ish values
189	
190	    D = _run_tile(mod, A, B, N, k_steps)        # [64,16]
191	    Dref = _reference(A, B)                      # D[m,n] = B[n,m] for m<16
192	    err = _max_err(D, Dref)
193	    assert err < _ATOL, (
194	        f"A=I localization FAILED max_err={err:.3e} — fragment-layout / "
195	        f"descriptor / transpose bug. D[:4,:4]=\n{D[:4,:4].cpu()}\n"
196	        f"ref[:4,:4]=\n{Dref[:4,:4]}")
197	    print(f"[gate-localization] A=I  N={N} max_err={err:.3e}  OK")

60	from dataclasses import dataclass, field

63	import torch

65	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
66	# Architecture constants (single source — mirrored by the C++ layout header and
67	# the codegen). These are the decoder cell's fixed shapes in the grokking race.
68	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
69	VOCAB = 99      # num_tokens (DEFAULT_CONFIG["num_tokens"]) — token range [0,98]
70	D_MODEL = 128   # dim_model (MODEL_SCALES["small"])
71	N_HEADS = 4     # num_heads
72	N_LAYERS = 2    # num_layers
73	SEQ = 4         # _raw_model hardcodes seq=4 for the decoder (make_data → 4 toks)
74	D_FF = 4 * D_MODEL  # 512 — ff hidden (Linear(d,4*d))
75	D_HEAD = D_MODEL // N_HEADS  # 32
76	LN_EPS = 1e-5   # torch.nn.LayerNorm default eps
77	ATTN_SCALE = 1.0 / math.sqrt(D_HEAD)  # 1/sqrt(32)
78	
79	
80	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
81	# Exact-erf GELU and its derivative (the REAL nn.GELU(), NOT the tanh approx).
82	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
83	_INV_SQRT2 = 1.0 / math.sqrt(2.0)
84	_INV_SQRT_2PI = 1.0 / math.sqrt(2.0 * math.pi)
85	
86	
87	def gelu(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
88	    return 0.5 * x * (1.0 + torch.erf(x * _INV_SQRT2))
89	
90	
91	def gelu_grad(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
92	    # d/dx [0.5 x (1+erf(x/sqrt2))] = 0.5(1+erf(x/sqrt2)) + x * phi(x),
93	    # phi(x) = (1/sqrt(2pi)) exp(-x^2/2)  (the normal pdf).
94	    cdf = 0.5 * (1.0 + torch.erf(x * _INV_SQRT2))
95	    pdf = _INV_SQRT_2PI * torch.exp(-0.5 * x * x)
96	    return cdf + x * pdf
97	
98	
99	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
100	# LayerNorm fwd/bwd (eps=1e-5), over the last dim (size d). Affine (gamma,beta).
101	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
102	def layernorm_forward(x, gamma, beta, eps=LN_EPS):
103	    """x: [..., d]. Returns (y, cache) where cache has the bwd intermediates."""
104	    mu = x.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
105	    xc = x - mu
106	    var = (xc * xc).mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
107	    inv_std = 1.0 / torch.sqrt(var + eps)
108	    xhat = xc * inv_std
109	    y = xhat * gamma + beta
110	    return y, (xhat, inv_std, gamma)
111	
112	
113	def layernorm_backward(dy, cache):
114	    """Returns (dx, dgamma, dbeta). dgamma/dbeta summed over all but last dim."""
115	    xhat, inv_std, gamma = cache
116	    d = xhat.shape[-1]
117	    # Reduce gamma/beta grads over every leading (batch/seq) axis.
118	    reduce_axes = tuple(range(dy.dim() - 1))
119	    dbeta = dy.sum(dim=reduce_axes)
120	    dgamma = (dy * xhat).sum(dim=reduce_axes)
121	    dxhat = dy * gamma
122	    # Standard LN dx: (1/d) * inv_std * (d*dxhat - sum(dxhat) - xhat*sum(dxhat*xhat))
123	    sum_dxhat = dxhat.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
124	    sum_dxhat_xhat = (dxhat * xhat).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
125	    dx = inv_std * (dxhat - (sum_dxhat + xhat * sum_dxhat_xhat) / d)
126	    return dx, dgamma, dbeta

128	
129	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
130	# Softmax over the last dim with row-max subtraction (matches torch), + bwd.
131	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
132	def softmax_lastdim(x):
133	    m = x.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
134	    e = torch.exp(x - m)
135	    s = e.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
136	    return e / s
137	
138	
139	def softmax_backward(dy, y):
140	    # dx = y * (dy - sum(dy*y))  (over the softmax axis).
141	    s = (dy * y).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
142	    return y * (dy - s)

147	# The CUDA flat-buffer offsets are generated from this same order (see
148	# decoder_param_layout()).

150	# (name, shape) in the EXACT order torch's named_parameters() yields them. This
151	# is THE single source of truth for the flat weight layout; the C++ header
152	# (csrc/fused/sm_90/decoder_layout.cuh) static-asserts the count + total.
153	def decoder_param_spec() -> List[Tuple[str, Tuple[int, ...]]]:
154	    spec: List[Tuple[str, Tuple[int, ...]]] = [
155	        ("tok.weight", (VOCAB, D_MODEL)),
156	        ("pos.weight", (SEQ, D_MODEL)),
157	    ]
158	    for li in range(N_LAYERS):
159	        p = f"layers.{li}."
160	        spec += [
161	            (p + "attn.in_proj_weight", (3 * D_MODEL, D_MODEL)),
162	            (p + "attn.in_proj_bias", (3 * D_MODEL,)),
163	            (p + "attn.out_proj.weight", (D_MODEL, D_MODEL)),
164	            (p + "attn.out_proj.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
165	            (p + "n1.weight", (D_MODEL,)),
166	            (p + "n1.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
167	            (p + "n2.weight", (D_MODEL,)),
168	            (p + "n2.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
169	            (p + "ff.0.weight", (D_FF, D_MODEL)),
170	            (p + "ff.0.bias", (D_FF,)),
171	            (p + "ff.2.weight", (D_MODEL, D_FF)),
172	            (p + "ff.2.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
173	        ]
174	    spec += [
175	        ("norm.weight", (D_MODEL,)),
176	        ("norm.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
177	        ("out.weight", (VOCAB, D_MODEL)),
178	        ("out.bias", (VOCAB,)),
179	    ]
180	    return spec

182	
183	def decoder_param_layout() -> Dict[str, object]:
184	    """Flat-buffer layout: offsets/sizes per tensor (the megakernel ABI view).
185	
186	    Returns dict with: names, offsets (elements into the flat buffer), sizes,
187	    total (== 422755), n_tensors (== 30). The offsets follow named_parameters()
188	    order so the flat blob == torch.cat([p.reshape(-1) for _, p in
189	    model.named_parameters()]).
190	    """
191	    spec = decoder_param_spec()
192	    names, offsets, sizes = [], [], []
193	    off = 0
194	    for name, shape in spec:
195	        n = 1
196	        for s in shape:
197	            n *= s
198	        names.append(name)
199	        offsets.append(off)
200	        sizes.append(n)
201	        off += n
202	    return dict(names=names, offsets=offsets, sizes=sizes, shapes=[s for _, s in spec],
203	                total=off, n_tensors=len(spec))
204	
205	
206	@dataclass
207	class DecoderWeights:
208	    """All 30 decoder weights as named tensors. Built either from a flat buffer
209	    (the megakernel view) or from a torch nn module's named_parameters()."""
210	    tok: torch.Tensor
211	    pos: torch.Tensor
212	    layers: List[Dict[str, torch.Tensor]]
213	    norm_w: torch.Tensor
214	    norm_b: torch.Tensor
215	    out_w: torch.Tensor
216	    out_b: torch.Tensor
217	
218	    @staticmethod
219	    def from_named(named: Dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> "DecoderWeights":
220	        layers = []
221	        for li in range(N_LAYERS):
222	            p = f"layers.{li}."
223	            layers.append(dict(
224	                in_w=named[p + "attn.in_proj_weight"],
225	                in_b=named[p + "attn.in_proj_bias"],
226	                out_w=named[p + "attn.out_proj.weight"],
227	                out_b=named[p + "attn.out_proj.bias"],
228	                n1_w=named[p + "n1.weight"], n1_b=named[p + "n1.bias"],
229	                n2_w=named[p + "n2.weight"], n2_b=named[p + "n2.bias"],
230	                ff0_w=named[p + "ff.0.weight"], ff0_b=named[p + "ff.0.bias"],
231	                ff2_w=named[p + "ff.2.weight"], ff2_b=named[p + "ff.2.bias"],
232	            ))
233	        return DecoderWeights(
234	            tok=named["tok.weight"], pos=named["pos.weight"], layers=layers,
235	            norm_w=named["norm.weight"], norm_b=named["norm.bias"],
236	            out_w=named["out.weight"], out_b=named["out.bias"])
237	
238	    @staticmethod
239	    def from_flat(flat: torch.Tensor) -> "DecoderWeights":
240	        lay = decoder_param_layout()
241	        named = {}
242	        for name, off, sz, shape in zip(lay["names"], lay["offsets"],
243	                                        lay["sizes"], lay["shapes"]):
244	            named[name] = flat[off:off + sz].reshape(shape)
245	        return DecoderWeights.from_named(named)
246	
247	
248	def _causal_mask(seq: int, device, dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
249	    """Additive mask [seq, seq]: 0 where j<=i, -inf where j>i (triu diag=1)."""
250	    m = torch.triu(torch.ones(seq, seq, dtype=torch.bool, device=device), 1)
251	    add = torch.zeros(seq, seq, device=device, dtype=dtype)
252	    add = add.masked_fill(m, float("-inf"))
253	    return add
254	
255	
256	# ===========================================================================
257	#  FORWARD (manual, primitive ops) — caches everything the manual backward needs.
258	# ===========================================================================
259	def decoder_forward(W: DecoderWeights, tokens: torch.Tensor,
260	                    targets: torch.Tensor):
261	    """tokens: [B, SEQ] int64 in [0, VOCAB). targets: [B] int64.
262	
263	    Returns (loss_scalar, cache). loss = mean-over-batch cross-entropy on the
264	    LAST-position logits. cache holds every fwd intermediate for the backward.
265	    """
266	    B, S = tokens.shape
267	    device, dtype = W.tok.device, W.tok.dtype
268	    add_mask = _causal_mask(S, device, dtype)  # [S,S]
269	
270	    # Embedding + positional. pos_ids = arange(S).
271	    pos_ids = torch.arange(S, device=device)
272	    h = W.tok[tokens] + W.pos[pos_ids].unsqueeze(0)   # [B,S,d]
273	
274	    layer_caches = []
275	    for li in range(N_LAYERS):
276	        L = W.layers[li]
277	        x_in = h  # residual base for the attention sublayer
278	        # ----- self-attention (MultiheadAttention semantics) -----
279	        qkv = x_in @ L["in_w"].t() + L["in_b"]        # [B,S,3d]
280	        q, k, v = qkv.split(D_MODEL, dim=-1)
281	        # split heads: [B,S,d] -> [B,h,S,dh]
282	        def sh(t):
283	            return t.reshape(B, S, N_HEADS, D_HEAD).permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
284	        qh, kh, vh = sh(q), sh(k), sh(v)
285	        scores = (qh @ kh.transpose(-2, -1)) * ATTN_SCALE   # [B,h,S,S]
286	        scores = scores + add_mask                          # causal
287	        attn = softmax_lastdim(scores)                      # [B,h,S,S]
288	        ctxh = attn @ vh                                     # [B,h,S,dh]
289	        ctx = ctxh.permute(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, S, D_MODEL)  # merge heads
290	        a = ctx @ L["out_w"].t() + L["out_b"]               # [B,S,d]
291	        # ----- residual + n1 (POST-LN): x = n1(x_in + a) -----
292	        r1 = x_in + a
293	        x1, ln1_cache = layernorm_forward(r1, L["n1_w"], L["n1_b"])
294	        # ----- FFN: ff2(gelu(ff0(x1))) -----
295	        ff0 = x1 @ L["ff0_w"].t() + L["ff0_b"]              # [B,S,4d]
296	        g = gelu(ff0)                                        # [B,S,4d]
297	        ff2 = g @ L["ff2_w"].t() + L["ff2_b"]              # [B,S,d]
298	        # ----- residual + n2 (POST-LN): h = n2(x1 + ff2) -----
299	        r2 = x1 + ff2
300	        h2, ln2_cache = layernorm_forward(r2, L["n2_w"], L["n2_b"])
301	        layer_caches.append(dict(
302	            x_in=x_in, qkv=qkv, qh=qh, kh=kh, vh=vh, attn=attn, ctxh=ctxh,
303	            ctx=ctx, r1=r1, x1=x1, ln1_cache=ln1_cache, ff0=ff0, g=g, r2=r2,
304	            ln2_cache=ln2_cache))
305	        h = h2
306	
307	    # Final norm + head on the LAST position only.
308	    h_last = h[:, -1, :]                                   # [B,d]
309	    hn, norm_cache = layernorm_forward(h_last, W.norm_w, W.norm_b)
310	    logits = hn @ W.out_w.t() + W.out_b                    # [B,VOCAB]
311	    # Cross-entropy, mean over batch (numerically-stable log-softmax).
312	    m = logits.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
313	    logz = m.squeeze(-1) + torch.log(torch.exp(logits - m).sum(dim=-1))
314	    nll = logz - logits.gather(1, targets.unsqueeze(1)).squeeze(1)
315	    loss = nll.mean()
316	    cache = dict(B=B, S=S, tokens=tokens, targets=targets,
317	                 layer_caches=layer_caches, h_last=h_last, hn=hn,
318	                 norm_cache=norm_cache, logits=logits, add_mask=add_mask)
319	    return loss, cache
320	
321	
322	# ===========================================================================
323	#  BACKWARD (manual, NO autograd) — returns grads for every named parameter.
324	# ===========================================================================
325	def decoder_backward(W: DecoderWeights, cache) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
326	    B, S = cache["B"], cache["S"]
327	    targets = cache["targets"]
328	    tokens = cache["tokens"]
329	    grads: Dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
330	
331	    # ----- CE backward: dlogits = (softmax - onehot) / B -----
332	    logits = cache["logits"]
333	    sm = softmax_lastdim(logits)                           # [B,VOCAB]
334	    onehot = torch.zeros_like(sm)
335	    onehot.scatter_(1, targets.unsqueeze(1), 1.0)
336	    dlogits = (sm - onehot) / B                            # [B,VOCAB]
337	
338	    # ----- head (out): logits = hn @ out_w^T + out_b -----
339	    hn = cache["hn"]                                       # [B,d]
340	    grads["out.weight"] = dlogits.t() @ hn                 # [VOCAB,d]
341	    grads["out.bias"] = dlogits.sum(dim=0)                 # [VOCAB]
342	    dhn = dlogits @ W.out_w                                # [B,d]
343	
344	    # ----- final norm backward -----
345	    dh_last, dnorm_w, dnorm_b = layernorm_backward(dhn, cache["norm_cache"])
346	    grads["norm.weight"] = dnorm_w
347	    grads["norm.bias"] = dnorm_b
348	
349	    # Upstream into the last layer's output: only the LAST position has grad.
350	    dh = torch.zeros(B, S, D_MODEL, device=hn.device, dtype=hn.dtype)
351	    dh[:, -1, :] = dh_last
352	
353	    # ----- per-layer backward (reverse) -----
354	    for li in reversed(range(N_LAYERS)):
355	        L = W.layers[li]
356	        lc = cache["layer_caches"][li]
357	        gp = f"layers.{li}."
358	        # h2 = n2(r2);  dh is grad wrt h2.
359	        dr2, dn2_w, dn2_b = layernorm_backward(dh, lc["ln2_cache"])
360	        grads[gp + "n2.weight"] = dn2_w
361	        grads[gp + "n2.bias"] = dn2_b
362	        # r2 = x1 + ff2  -> grad flows to x1 (residual) AND ff2.
363	        dff2 = dr2
364	        dx1 = dr2.clone()
365	        # ff2 = g @ ff2_w^T + ff2_b
366	        g = lc["g"]                                        # [B,S,4d]
367	        grads[gp + "ff.2.weight"] = (dff2.reshape(-1, D_MODEL).t()

def _disable_tf32():
    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
    torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False


def _k_scaled_atol(K):
    # fp32 accumulation-order bound ≈ K·ε·scale with ε=2^-24. Unit-scale random
    # operands, well-conditioned. Substrate used 2e-3 at K<=512; scale linearly
    # with a floor. (This is the bf16-rounded-oracle accumulation-order gate; the
    # bf16 input noise cancels because both sides are bf16-rounded.)
    return max(2e-3, 2e-3 * (K / 512.0))


# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  PART 1 — GEMM orientation micro-gates.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def _bf16(t):
    return t.to(torch.bfloat16)


@_GATE
def test_fwd_identity_localization():
    """(fwd) A=I localization: X = [I | 0] (TILE_M x Kin, first Kin rows identity
    over the K=Kin cols) ⇒ Y[m,n] = W[n,m] for m<Kin. Isolates fragment-layout /
    descriptor / TILE_M-stacking bugs."""
    mod = _build_module()
    _disable_tf32()
    TILE_M = mod.TILE_M
    N, Kin = 128, 128
    X = torch.zeros(TILE_M, Kin, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
    for i in range(min(Kin, TILE_M)):
        X[i, i] = 1.0
    W = (torch.arange(N * Kin, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32).reshape(N, Kin) / 97.0)
    Xb, Wb = _bf16(X), _bf16(W)
    D = mod.gemm_fwd(Xb.reshape(-1).contiguous(), Wb.reshape(-1).contiguous(), N, Kin)
    # ref: Y[m,n] = Σ_k Xb[m,k]·Wb[n,k]
    ref = torch.einsum("mk,nk->mn", Xb.double().cpu(), Wb.double().cpu())
    err = (D.double().cpu() - ref).abs().max().item()
    assert err < _k_scaled_atol(Kin), (
        f"fwd A=I localization max_err={err:.3e} — layout/descriptor/stacking bug\n"
        f"D[:4,:4]=\n{D[:4,:4].cpu()}\nref[:4,:4]=\n{ref[:4,:4]}")
    print(f"[fwd-loc] A=I TILE_M={TILE_M} N={N} K={Kin} max_err={err:.3e}  OK")


@_GATE
@pytest.mark.parametrize("Kin", [128, 512])
def test_fwd_random(Kin):
    """(fwd) random X,W over the design's K depths (in/out K=128, ff2 K=512)."""
    mod = _build_module()
    _disable_tf32()
    TILE_M = mod.TILE_M
    N = 128
    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(1000 + Kin)
    X = torch.randn(TILE_M, Kin, generator=g, device="cuda")
    W = torch.randn(N, Kin, generator=g, device="cuda")
    Xb, Wb = _bf16(X), _bf16(W)
    D = mod.gemm_fwd(Xb.reshape(-1).contiguous(), Wb.reshape(-1).contiguous(), N, Kin)
    ref = torch.einsum("mk,nk->mn", Xb.double().cpu(), Wb.double().cpu())
    err = (D.double().cpu() - ref).abs().max().item()
    tol = _k_scaled_atol(Kin) * max(1.0, ref.abs().max().item())
    assert err < tol, f"fwd random K={Kin} max_err={err:.3e} tol={tol:.3e}"
    print(f"[fwd] random N={N} K={Kin} max_err={err:.3e} tol={tol:.3e}  OK")


@_GATE
@pytest.mark.parametrize("Nout", [128, 512])
def test_dx_random(Nout):
    """(dX) dX = dY @ W with W TRANSPOSED-staged. N(wgmma)=in_dim=128, K=Nout
    (in_proj-dX has Nout=3d=384; out_proj 128; ff0-dX Nout=dff=512; ff2-dX 128).
    Exercises Nout in {128 (out/ff2), 512 (ff0)} — the transposed-W orientation."""
    mod = _build_module()
    _disable_tf32()
    TILE_M = mod.TILE_M
    N = 128                                   # in_dim
    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(2000 + Nout)
    dY = torch.randn(TILE_M, Nout, generator=g, device="cuda")
    W = torch.randn(Nout, N, generator=g, device="cuda")   # [Nout, in_dim]
    dYb, Wb = _bf16(dY), _bf16(W)
    D = mod.gemm_dx(dYb.reshape(-1).contiguous(), Wb.reshape(-1).contiguous(), N, Nout)
    # ref dX[m,i] = Σ_o dY[m,o]·W[o,i]
    ref = torch.einsum("mo,oi->mi", dYb.double().cpu(), Wb.double().cpu())
    err = (D.double().cpu() - ref).abs().max().item()
    tol = _k_scaled_atol(Nout) * max(1.0, ref.abs().max().item())
    assert err < tol, f"dX Nout={Nout} max_err={err:.3e} tol={tol:.3e}"
    print(f"[dX] random N={N} Nout(K)={Nout} max_err={err:.3e} tol={tol:.3e}  OK")


@_GATE
@pytest.mark.parametrize("T", [128, 2048])
def test_dw_random_multistep(T):
    """(dW) dW = dY^T @ X with BOTH operands TRANSPOSED-staged, K=T multi-k-step.
    THE stride-bug gate (model_stages_decoder.cuh:619-625 lesson): a single tile
    would pass with a wrong k-stride. T=2048 = 128 k-steps. Nout=128 (out_proj
    weight class), in_dim N=128."""
    mod = _build_module()
    _disable_tf32()
    Nout, N = 128, 128
    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(3000 + T)
    dY = torch.randn(T, Nout, generator=g, device="cuda")     # [T, out]
    X = torch.randn(T, N, generator=g, device="cuda")         # [T, in]
    dYb, Xb = _bf16(dY), _bf16(X)
    D = mod.gemm_dw(dYb.reshape(-1).contiguous(), Xb.reshape(-1).contiguous(), N, Nout, T)
    ref = torch.einsum("to,ti->oi", dYb.double().cpu(), Xb.double().cpu())
    err = (D.double().cpu() - ref).abs().max().item()
    tol = _k_scaled_atol(T) * max(1.0, ref.abs().max().item())
    assert err < tol, f"dW T(K)={T} max_err={err:.3e} tol={tol:.3e}"
    print(f"[dW] random Nout={Nout} in={N} K=T={T} ({T//16} steps) "
          f"max_err={err:.3e} tol={tol:.3e}  OK")


@_GATE
def test_dw_identity_who_owns_what():
    """(dW) A=I-style: dY = [I_Nout | 0] over T rows (dY[t,o]=1 iff t==o for
    t<Nout else 0). Then dW[o,i] = Σ_t dY[t,o]·X[t,i] = X[o,i] for o<Nout. Pins
    the (out,t)->fragment mapping for the doubly-transposed staging."""
    mod = _build_module()
    _disable_tf32()
    Nout, N, T = 128, 128, 256
    dY = torch.zeros(T, Nout, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
    for o in range(min(Nout, T)):
        dY[o, o] = 1.0
    X = (torch.arange(T * N, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32).reshape(T, N) / 131.0)
    dYb, Xb = _bf16(dY), _bf16(X)
    D = mod.gemm_dw(dYb.reshape(-1).contiguous(), Xb.reshape(-1).contiguous(), N, Nout, T)
    ref = Xb[:Nout, :].double().cpu()      # dW[o,i] = X[o,i]
    err = (D.double().cpu() - ref).abs().max().item()
    assert err < _k_scaled_atol(T), (
        f"dW A=I localization max_err={err:.3e} — transposed-staging mapping bug\n"
        f"D[:4,:4]=\n{D[:4,:4].cpu()}\nref[:4,:4]=\n{ref[:4,:4]}")
    print(f"[dW-loc] A=I Nout={Nout} in={N} T={T} max_err={err:.3e}  OK")


@_GATE
def test_determinism_bitwise():
    """Same inputs twice → bit-identical (fixed tile + ascending-k, no atomics)."""
    mod = _build_module()
    _disable_tf32()
    Nout, N, T = 128, 128, 512
    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(31337)
    dY = _bf16(torch.randn(T, Nout, generator=g, device="cuda")).reshape(-1).contiguous()
    X = _bf16(torch.randn(T, N, generator=g, device="cuda")).reshape(-1).contiguous()
    D1 = mod.gemm_dw(dY, X, N, Nout, T)
    D2 = mod.gemm_dw(dY, X, N, Nout, T)
    D3 = mod.gemm_dw(dY, X, N, Nout, T)
    assert torch.equal(D1, D2) and torch.equal(D2, D3), "non-deterministic dW"
    print("[determinism] dW A/A/A bit-identical  OK")


# ── direct-run report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _main():
    if not _sm90a_available():
        print("SKIP: no sm_90 GPU.")
        return 0
    print("Building decoder TC self-test (JIT, sm_90a)…")
    _build_module()
    fails = []

    def _try(name, fn, *a):
        try:
            fn(*a)
        except Exception as e:
            fails.append((name, repr(e)))
            print(f"  [FAIL] {name}: {e!r}")

    _try("fwd-loc(A=I)", test_fwd_identity_localization)
    for K in (128, 512):
        _try(f"fwd random K={K}", test_fwd_random, K)
    for Nout in (128, 512):
        _try(f"dX random Nout={Nout}", test_dx_random, Nout)
    for T in (128, 2048):
        _try(f"dW random T={T}", test_dw_random_multistep, T)
    _try("dW-loc(A=I)", test_dw_identity_who_owns_what)
    _try("determinism", test_determinism_bitwise)

    print("\n==================== SUMMARY ====================")
    if not fails:
        print("ALL PART-1 GEMM-ORIENTATION GATES PASSED")
        return 0
    print(f"{len(fails)} FAILURE(S):")
    for n, e in fails:
        print(f"  - {n}: {e}")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(_main())
